Peter,

Today marks the fifth anniversary of January 6, 2021—the day a violent mob, encouraged by Donald Trump, tried to overturn the results of a free and fair election. And the truth is, _the threat hasn't gone away._

Kim has been hearing from people all across our district—whether they've come to a town hall, called Kim's office, or written in response to one of her emails—that they are scared for what's to come of our democracy under the leadership of Donald Trump and his GOP yes men.

And, frankly, **they have good reason to be.**

Look at the pattern we're seeing unfold from Donald Trump since he took office again last January:
* Silencing media outlets and attacking anyone who refuses to stand behind him and his reckless agenda—directly undermining the First Amendment.
* Directing his Attorney General to target and sue political opponents in an effort to intimidate and silence opposition.
* Attacking vote-by-mail and other measures that make it easier for people to cast their ballots.
* Defying court orders and threatening the independence of our judicial system, even going so far as to threaten states that don't align with his policies, and sidestepping state authority.

These are not isolated incidents, Peter.

Trump has gone out of his way both during his time in office and outside of it to fundamentally undermine our trust in the democratic process to set the stage for his self-serving, anti-American leadership.

Kim wants you to know that she's been listening, and that in the House, she's doing everything she can to fight back and ensure that your concerns are being prioritized by someone who shares them. But we have to go the extra mile and elect a blue Congress this November to ensure our system of checks and balances is back in place.

Certifying the presidential election on January 6, 2025, was one of the most challenging moments in my career.

Peter -
Five years ago, an armed mob stormed the United States Capitol. Inspired by lies and hatred spewed by Donald Trump, they used brutal violence and intimidation in an attempt to overturn a free and fair election. And since returning to office, Trump pardoned the insurrectionists who betrayed their country.
January 6, 2021, showed us how fragile our democracy is.
We, the people, must fight back against Donald Trump and his cronies as they sow chaos and fear among the American people.
We cannot stand idly by as they strip our fundamental freedoms, enrich themselves on the back of working people, and destroy our reputation around the globe. And we must continue to do the hard work to ensure our democracy survives.
Let me be clear: Certifying the presidential election on January 6, 2025, was one of the most challenging moments in my career. Yet I never — not for one second — considered any other action.
Because the American people had spoken.
And in our nation, the power is and must always be with the people.
Kamala

name: Jocelyn Benson
subject: A day we can’t forget
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR
body:
Nothing can deter me from defending the Constitution and protecting the will of the people.
# [](https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/203?t=1&akid=1267%2E181023%2ELyotSl)
Hi there,
Five years ago today, the nation witnessed the assault on the U.S. Capitol — an assault on our democracy. The Jan 6 mob injured more than 150 Capitol and D.C. police officers. They called for the death of Vice President Mike Pence and stalked the U.S. Capitol’s hallways in an attempt to prevent the certification of a fair and legitimate presidential election.
_It happened because of lies._ Because of a choice leaders made to spread and repeat lies about our democracy. They spread and repeated those lies in court, to the media, in the halls of our state legislatures.
That wasn’t the only violent protest spurred by those lies. One night in December 2020, armed protesters descended on my home. Inside, my then 4-year-old son and I were decorating for the holidays. As we sheltered in place for the better part of an hour while we waited for the police to arrive, I was scared. But I was also determined to protect the voters of Michigan. And no one, no matter how powerful or threatening, was going to deter me from defending the Constitution and protecting the will of the people.
I am no less determined now. Last November, Donald Trump issued pardons to dozens of his allies who used lies, threats, and intimidation tactics to overturn the election. He had already pardoned the rioters convicted of using violence and threats in the Capitol attack, demonstrating that he has no respect for the rule of law or the will of the people.
This president believes that there is one justice system for those who do Trump’s bidding and another for the rest of us. His pardons signal a bright green light to anyone looking to disrupt, attack, or otherwise undermine free and fair elections in the future.
Michigan Republicans have taken the bait. Two statewide Republican candidates — one seeking the nomination for governor and the other for U.S. Senate — have repeated and amplified the president’s lies about the 2020 election. Nearly two dozen state Republican lawmakers last week asked Trump’s Justice Department to take over the administration of our state’s elections, citing misinformation and conspiracy theories.
We won’t let that happen again. In our state, attempts to sabotage election results will have consequences. People can still face criminal charges under state law and will still be held accountable in our state courts.
**In our democracy, the power of the people must always be greater than the people in power.** The 2026 elections are less than a year away. This is our chance to remind this president that his powers are not limitless, that there are indeed still checks and balances in this country. They come from state officials with the moral courage to hold the line and from the voters who refuse to be silenced.
We spend today remembering how a lie and an unwillingness to accept the will of the people led to tragedy at our U.S. Capitol.
And then we spend tomorrow and every day thereafter defending democracy and demanding consequences for all involved.
In solidarity,
Jocelyn

body:
The lies and attacks on vote-by-mail have only increased in the last 48 hours, Team. Trump's statement has brought all the usual anti-voting, anti-democracy suspects out of the woodwork to ramp up the falsehoods we've heard for years.
But we've also seen defenders of voting rights standing up for our fundamental right to vote. We've just got to make sure our grassroots power can match their dark money millions and suppressive media empire.
RUSH $25 or more right now to fuel our work in the states, in Congress, and in the courts to defend mail-in voting and make every vote count in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=010626_2&amount=25]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
ABC: Trump says he will lead 'movement' to end mail-in voting [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=010626_2&amount=25]
Our time in the barrel has come, Team .
President Donald Trump said just hours ago that he will lead a "movement" to get rid of mail-in ballots and voting machines , falsely claiming that they lead to voter fraud.
Word for lying word: " I am going to lead a movement to get rid of MAIL-IN BALLOTS, and also, while we're at it, Highly 'Inaccurate,' Very Expensive, and Seriously Controversial VOTING MACHINES, which cost Ten Times more than accurate and sophisticated Watermark Paper, which is faster, and leaves NO DOUBT, at the end of the evening, as to who WON, and who LOST, the Election. "
How is Trump going to do this? He's signing an executive order ahead of next year's critical midterms. Is this just another attempt to distract from a failing economy, rising prices, and his role in the Epstein scandal? Probably, yes. Are we going to fight him tooth and nail? You betcha.
We're going to work in the states to defend our access to cast ballots, as they run elections. We're going to petition members of Congress to stop harmful bills that might attempt to back up this executive order. And we're going to do everything we can to support the efforts to stop this in court.
We'll be blunt: We still need your help to protect our fundamental right to vote. Chip in with $25 or whatever you can today to defend vote by mail across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=010626_2&amount=25]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

Trump has long lied about mail-in voting. He's claimed mail-in voting contributed to his 2020 election loss, though no widespread fraud has been found. In fact, the one case of mail-in ballot fraud in Pennsylvania after the 2020 election was a man who was prosecuted for returning his dead mother's ballot for Trump .
We all know just how safe and secure mail-in voting is. It's use dates back to the Civil War. The use of mail-in voting has become very common across the country and study after study has shown that fraud in mail-ballot voting is rare. There are also several safeguards in place nationwide to protect against fraud, including signature requirements and barcodes to track envelopes sent by officials. States have spent tens of millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing.
Being blunt: There is no good-faith reason to limit vote-by-mail access. There is no good-faith reason to end the use of mail-in voting, or do the other things in this forthcoming executive order or his previous one attacking vote-by-mail. Just like the wave of redistricting efforts in Texas, Florida, and beyond -- this is a partisan voter suppression exercise meant to codify MAGA's power in perpetuity and end our democracy.
Opponents of voting rights will go to any length necessary to stop people from voting and stay in power. Help us fight back with $25 or whatever you can to protect mail-in voting and stop their suppressive policies >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=010626_2&amount=25]

https://www.facebook.com/voteraction [https://www.facebook.com/voteraction] https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org [https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org] https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/ [https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/] https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/ [https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/]
Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=010626_2&amount=20]

name: Mark Kelly
subject: They can threaten my rank and my pension — but they’re not going to shut me up
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Gillen for NY
body:
You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.

| Peter:

Pete Hegseth decided he's going to censure me, and is threatening to demote me and reduce my pension.

I got shot at in service to this country. I missed holidays and birthdays. I commanded a space shuttle mission and launched to the International Space Station while my wife recovered from a gunshot wound to the head.

My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like.

You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.

body:

Introduction from Alex
Hello! For those of you who aren’t familiar with me or with this campaign: my name is Alex Kelloff, and I’m the sole Democratic candidate for Colorado’s 3rd district. Our campaign’s been running since April of last year, and I hope you’ll follow along as we enter 2026.
I hope everyone had an excellent holiday break. I know I’m excited to be in 2026 and am looking ahead to the major task we have ahead of us — to put this seat in the hands of an elected representative who will represent “we the people” instead of being captured by this Administration. I decided to run for Congress because when Donald Trump was re-elected I was deeply concerned about where he’d take our country. I think this last year saw that fear borne out for many of us. I frequently ask constituents on the campaign trail: Do you feel better off today than you did just a year ago? My answer, and many of those I ask, is a resounding “NO.”
Already we’re seeing what this year will likely bring — continued chaos as exemplified by the Administration’s actions in Venezuela this past weekend. Based on Trump and Congress’ actions since taking office, which will hurt America’s long-term interests, Republicans in Congress are going to feel the walls closing in, as they know the Midterms will hand them a major loss. As the Midterms draw closer, we know the Administration will lash out and try to distract people from their failed policies.
Our job is to stay focused — to deliver on what people actually need. In Colorado’s 3rd District, that’s creating good jobs and reducing the cost of living. If elected, I will fight to keep our rural hospitals open by securing Medicaid funding, work to expand our housing supply so that people can afford to live here, and keep costs low at the grocery store by reigning in tariffs and supporting our farmers. That’s why I want to go to Congress: to make people’s lives better here in Colorado. We can do this but we need real leadership to make it happen.
Thank you for your support of my campaign.
— Alex
2025 Recap:
In 2025, our campaign showed up. We visited all 27 counties across Colorado’s 3rd District, driving more than 15,525 miles to meet people where they live and work. Along the way, we held 162 meetings and participated in 77 in-person events — listening, learning, and building real connections in communities large and small. That work earned the support of 21 endorsements , reflecting a growing coalition united around putting people first and delivering real results for Southern and Western Colorado.
At the end of the day, it’s about the people — the conversations and communities that define Colorado’s 3rd District. I am thankful for every conversation, every cup of coffee, and every mile traveled. We are proud of what we have started but now the real work begins in 2026.

Holding Hurd Accountable
Venezuela Intervention: Jeff Hurd supported the Administration’s actions and I can respect that on the basis that Nicolás Maduro ruled Venezuela without democratic legitimacy, oversaw years of repression of his own people, and likely supported actions and groups that harmed Americans and U.S. interests.
Nevertheless, our move against Maduro raises a number of questions as to what the U.S. is seeking to gain with his arrest. The Trump Administration’s indictment against Maduro asserts that his regime participated in drug trafficking. I am sure this is true, and I hope and expect that Maduro will be held fully accountable.
However, any reasonable American must ask — why the Trump Administration saw fit to pardon the convicted and incarcerated former President of Honduras, Juan Orlando Hernández, in December 2025. Hernández was convicted in June 2024 in a U.S. federal court with conspiracy to transport cocaine into the U.S., among other crimes. He was sentenced to 45 years in U.S. prison. Hernández’s charges are essentially the same charges that Maduro is currently being indicted on. Trump’s pardon of Hernández makes absolutely no sense.
Jeff Hurd has never mentioned the pardon of Hernández. Hurd’s hypocrisy is deafening!
Arkansas Valley Conduit Bill Veto By Trump: Hurd expressed that he was “deeply disappointed by the President’s veto of the Arkansas Valley Conduit legislation.” But being “disappointed” isn’t leadership. When a bipartisan, unanimous bill is vetoed by Trump and our rural communities are left without clean drinking water, Coloradans deserve more than a statement — they deserve real action, by real leaders.
Craig Station Extension Jeff Hurd recently praised the Department of Energy for ordering the coal plant, Craig Station, to remain open for 3 additional months until March 30, 2026. The order is “renewable, if needed.” Therefore, who really knows how long it will stay open?
Here is the truth: individuals, families and businesspeople can deal with adversity, but what they have a harder time dealing with is uncertainty. Craig Station is 47 years old and is unprofitable. If Craig Station is to stay open, the owner, Tri-State Generation and Transmission Association will have to make major investments, likely worth tens of millions of $$$, to keep it operating (by the way, it is not currently operating because it broke down in December). And if these investments are made, all customers' utility bills would go up to share in the costs of keeping the plant open.
Craig Station workers and coal miners who support the plant deserve better. They don’t deserve to be used as political pawns. They deserve certainty about their future so that they can make decisions for themselves and their families. And they deserve government support to help them retrain and transition into new, good paying jobs. Lastly, they deserve their government to be thoughtful and creative in replacing coal plants in Colorado with new energy generating plants that take advantage of the utility infrastructure already in-place and which can ensure lower utility costs for all customers going forward, while at the same time producing cleaner electricity.
Rather than playing partisan politics for good sound bites, Jeff Hurd should be developing real solutions that help Craig’s coal plant workers and miners, and put them on a path to long-term, sustainable jobs that they can be sure will exist for years to come.

Team Nunn ("JFC") is a joint fundraising committee composed of Iowans for Zach Nunn ("Campaign"), Call to Service PAC ("LPAC") and NRCC (each, a "Committee," and, collectively, the "Committees"). Any contribution to the JFC permissible under the Federal Election Campaign Act, as amended ("FECA"), from contributors who have not exceeded their applicable federal contribution limits, shall be allocated among the Committees pursuant to FECA and the formula set forth in this Notice.

_**Contributions Made by an Individual or Federal Non-Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Individuals or federal non-multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $322,100. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:

name: Deb Haaland
subject: My love letter to New Mexico
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
Looking back at what we've accomplished together

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=6712%2E400544%2ErZmlvg)
---
Friend, today marks New Mexico's 114th birthday! As someone who is proudly of and for New Mexico, I'm thrilled to celebrate our state, its incredible public lands, and most importantly, the caring, determined, passionate spirit of our people.
New Mexico is home to some of the most beautiful places, delicious food, and vibrant, diverse culture of anywhere in the world. **I'm honored today to not just celebrate our past, but also to lead the fight for our future.**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/3345?refcode=jtk119-fr-nd&t=2&akid=6712%2E400544%2ErZmlvg)
---
I'm running for governor to be a leader for all New Mexicans. That's why I've spent the past 11 months traveling to every corner of the state talking to as many people as I possibly can.
**And what have I learned?** For one, New Mexicans across our state have many similar concerns: rising costs of housing, access to healthcare, the future of our children, and the safety of our communities. We want to grow our clean energy economy, protect our precious public lands, and create educational opportunities for our children to thrive. These are just a few of the issues I will fight fiercely for starting on day one as our next governor.
Friend, I am proud to call New Mexico home. From my mother to my great-grandmother and many more before them, **I am blessed to come from 35 generations of resilient and fierce Pueblo women.** I grew up running through the desert with my cousins, graduated high school here in Albuquerque, ran a small business, and raised my child here. **I've never forgotten those roots and I never will. They shaped my values, my sense of responsibility, and my commitment to fight for the communities that raised me.**
**But the truth is I can't win this race without your help,****friend****.** The governor’s seat has a history of switching parties every eight years, and Republicans across the state have been gaining more registered voters. GOP donors are already preparing to spend millions to defeat me, and if we're going to buck the trend, I need you on my grassroots team.
**[So please, I am personally asking: Will you chip in anything at all today to help me become our next governor and create a better future for all New Mexicans?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/3345?refcode=jtk119-fr-nd&t=3&akid=6712%2E400544%2ErZmlvg)**
_If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_ | | | [Donate $10 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/3690?refcode=jtk119-fr-nd&t=4&akid=6712%2E400544%2ErZmlvg)
---
| | [Donate $35 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/3691?refcode=jtk119-fr-nd&t=5&akid=6712%2E400544%2ErZmlvg)
---
| | [Donate $50 >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/3692?refcode=jtk119-fr-nd&t=6&akid=6712%2E400544%2ErZmlvg)
---
| | [Other Amount >>](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/3693?refcode=jtk119-fr-nd&t=7&akid=6712%2E400544%2ErZmlvg)
---
Thank you for celebrating this special day with me, and thank you in advance for anything you're able to give. Together, I know we can win this race and make New Mexico the best it can be.

Stay fierce,

Deb
|

#

Five years ago, before dawn, we learned Rev. Warnock and I had won the Georgia Senate runoffs, securing the Senate majority.
Hours later, Trump’s mob sacked the Capitol, brutalized cops, hunted Pence and Pelosi, and tried to foil the peaceful transfer of power.
Returned to the presidency, Trump pardoned the thugs who did that violence for him and launched a dystopian campaign of official vengeance and intimidation unprecedented in our history.
You know all this.
You also know the stakes of these midterms.
Five years ago, it all came down to Georgia.
In **301 days,** when the polls close at 7 p.m., Georgia will be the political center of the universe again.
That’s because I’m the only Democratic Senator defending a seat in a state Trump won, and this will be the biggest Senate race of the year.
Look, I know you get a lot of fundraising emails — including from me.
But we just _have_ to win.
If we don’t restore checks and balances, if we don’t get out the vote, if we don’t defend voting rights over the next eleven months, we could lose our Republic.
This Senate race isn’t happening in November. It’s happening _right now._ The GOP is already spending big money in Georgia to defeat me.
I’m asking for your help. This is something you can do today that makes a difference.
[**Please send $5 or whatever you can to support my reelection campaign in Georgia.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-jan26.wPRyEn&refcode=em260106-2-subs&t=1&akid=1392%2E5691347%2E4gI2EA)

Fellow Patriot,

Happy New Year.

The Republican House majority is hanging by a thread. It’s one of the slimmest margins in modern history, and if we lose even a handful of seats, Democrats take the gavel back.

**If that happens, everything stops.**

No border security. No accountability. Just investigations, obstruction, and nonstop attacks on President Trump and the America First agenda. We’ve seen this movie before—and it ends badly.

I’m Mark Lamb, former Sheriff of Pinal County, Arizona. I spent years dealing with the consequences of Washington’s failures firsthand. Open borders aren’t theoretical to me. They mean drug trafficking, human trafficking, and communities paying the price while politicians in D.C. do nothing.

_That’s why I’m running for Congress._

This race matters nationally. Border security affects every state. The House majority affects every issue. **And the truth is, Democrats absolutely could flip the House if Republicans don’t get serious right now.**

**President Donald Trump endorsed this campaign because he knows I won’t fold, cave, or play games. I’ll fight for secure borders, law and order, and putting American citizens first.**

**But with margins this tight, winning takes more than endorsements. It takes a strong grassroots effort—and that starts now.**

It was 1993, on my Induction Day at the Naval Academy. I was so proud to be there, to have this chance to learn, work, and travel the world in service of my country. **The young woman in this photo never imagined she’d be a member of Congress.** She never imagined she’d be in the Capitol when it came under siege for the first time since the War of 1812. _Never_ in her wildest dreams did she expect to literally run for her life from a violent mob, or evacuate her office because a pipe bomb was discovered outside. She expected to face danger when she joined the Navy. But the danger didn’t come from enemy ships or nuclear submarines. It came from the most unthinkable place, from the Commander-in-Chief. I chose to serve on the January 6th Committee to hold the plotters accountable. I did so despite knowing it could cost me re-election. **I did it for the young woman in the photo who never wavered in her commitment to her country.** The truth is, we came within an inch of losing our democracy on January 6th. I’ll never forget what I witnessed that day, the extraordinary courage of our Capitol police and many of my colleagues—nor the extraordinary cowardice of our president and his co-conspirators. Today, I participated in a January 6th hearing on the Hill because I refuse to let the truth of that tragic day be buried. I will speak out. I will stand up. I will remind America that our freedoms are not free, that it takes courage to protect them. When we flip this district and put responsible patriots back in control of Congress, I’ll do everything in my power to defend your rights, protect your freedoms, and maintain the security of the United States. Forward,

subject: They can threaten my rank and my pension, but they’re not going to shut me up
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.
#

Team —
Pete Hegseth decided he's going to censure me, and is threatening to demote me and reduce my pension.
I got shot at in service to this country. I missed holidays and birthdays. I commanded a space shuttle mission and launched to the International Space Station while my wife recovered from a gunshot wound to the head.
My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like.
You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.
Pete Hegseth can threaten to reduce my rank and my pension. But I am not going to let him intimidate me, or anyone else. He is not going to stop me from defending our democracy from a president who is hellbent on destroying it.
If they think this is going to shut me up, they’ve got another thing coming.

Mark

Dear everyone —
Firstly, I want to thank you all for your commitment and support through 2025 — especially in the lead-up to our End-of-Year deadline on December 31st.
I am delighted to say that thanks to your support, we hit our fundraising goal and are well-positioned to go into 2026 and continue funding and expanding our organizing efforts in swing districts across the state.
Thank you. Thank you so much.
Additionally, I want to acknowledge today’s solemn anniversary.
Five years ago, Donald Trump’s lies about the validity of the 2020 Election fueled an insurrection at the U.S. Capitol. Today, we honor those who bravely defended the Capitol on January 6, 2021, and remember those who lost their lives protecting our democracy.
It’s been half a decade, but it also feels like it happened just yesterday.
Donald Trump’s continuous assaults on the foundations of our elections drove our democracy to the brink of ruin on January 6, 2021. In the last year, his chaotic administration has taken us back to the brink again and again.
That is why it is up to us to keep fighting for our democracy and everyone in it. Whether it’s protecting immigrants in the face of ICE raids, fighting for access to affordable health care, or expanding grassroots organizing to flip seats and take back the U.S. House Majority — we need you in this fight .
I know we can count on you in 2026. We’ll be in touch again soon.
Thank you,
Yvette Martinez
Executive Director

We have no choice but to hit our upcoming fundraising goal. Because if we fail, the Democrat Machine will crush us in every battleground district, barge back into power, and effectively BLOCKADE President Trump's entire legislative agenda.

| Together, we built something extraordinary in 2025.
Over 100,000 Democrats from every single state in the country rallied with Defend Our Courts to stop a MAGA takeover of Pennsylvania's Supreme Court.
The stakes could not have been higher. If MAGA had seized control, they would have locked in gerrymandering and rigged elections in the most important swing state in America.
If we had lost, MAGA would have opened Pandora's box on our democracy.
But Democrats like you answered the bell and we didn't just win, we blew MAGA out of the water by more than 30 points. Friend, you played no small part in that victory. In Philadelphia, where we concentrated much of our voter outreach along with digital and TV ads, turnout surged by 34 percent. That was the largest increase in the state. And it made the difference.
---

It was the biggest, most consequential Democratic victory of 2025.
And you were part of it, friend.
Now, we turn the page, and 2026 is already shaping up to be even more make-or-break for our democracy. Yes, control of Congress is on the line. But so is control of critical state supreme courts in Arizona, Georgia, and Michigan, with the same stakes on the line as PA.
The national party will be stretched thin competing for control of both the Senate and the House. So Defend Our Courts is preparing to step up to the plate again to lead the defense, build coalitions, scale our programs, and operate across three states at once.
In 2025, we proved that our strategy works. We have everything we need to meet this moment: the support, infrastructure, staff, and most importantly--you.
Friend, what we built in PA is too effective, too important to step away from. | Hi Peter -- I'm Mike Nelson -- a longtime news meteorologist and proud Coloradan.
After decades of tracking tornadoes, wildfires, floods and blizzards across our state, I've seen firsthand how timely, reliable weather reporting saves lives - especially in rural areas where help can be hours away.
But recently, Lauren Boebert and her friends in Congress have slashed critical weather and emergency preparedness funding. She backed the "Big, Beautiful Bill," which guts the systems we rely on to predict and prepare for extreme weather. That's not just irresponsible. It's dangerous.
That's why I'm standing with Trisha Calvarese. She actually grew up here. She knows our communities, shows up and listens. And she understands how important it is to protect the resources families count on - weather alerts, a reliable electric grid, emergency services.
We need someone in Congress who puts public safety before partisan soundbites. Someone who takes facts seriously and doesn't gamble with people's lives. ## Trump: Venezuela Shipping Oil to US
President Trump said Tuesday evening that Venezuelan officials will be turning over [between 30 million to 50 million barrels of oil](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdCDbGNspXKShu7Qp0YKXY6PFPoHvEPn6iBT5gTSjkUZ6o5nP23ADYkr3D1gxlDkPCY-dsRTchhcm_H4iQ8rEM5-U7hNsO6RBS21rqWrphgjE52CqGGZEjW2FQTnrnG_fpKqW4H000pjRedDT2GI3opHRtyM43RkDFYWLJpV0SknT-abtRm8BLFjUNsZJGImRSt6ar0ypLDjzmV-4NVNeKw5LKY9dtO9C90L3x3E0UxqnKxS6v9BC91JdcrmyPddH_beszsTNUlauthAfBzHTbp0w8r4C8W9D-dctr6B_AgAA__-DKHWT) to the United States. In a [Truth Social post](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO4yAQxvGnMV2iYWwDLihOOrnLVSdtaU1gHLPCYAFJlH36VfYVtv0-6Vf8Py7LhUIM6faPdrZtzUviZ43cGpflwYm_7hwp5RDX-Arp5qhUSgsCqhPIE-jFU4ivZRDerszIvWArtdLa9BNIsdkerw6Ux3X0fhoIpebJjD0adWXnQItg3xpI0FLCMJpzP16NIlKkGJX3rhuAfWi5nD9zSG3jNb7yg8vZ5V1Eu7V21K7_0-Hc4dzKvW01u0Dx_b_HAQpT_JsTRf-_3Pejw_nItdUOZylHM4KRWmujAJWZRLH-eIYYQ1W6G-C2U_ihRPtVn4fF7wAAAP__wW53-A), Trump said the oil will be sold at its market price, “and that money will be controlled by me, as President of the United States of America, to ensure it is used to benefit the people of Venezuela and the United States!” Trump said that the oil being turned over to the U.S. was “high-quality” and would otherwise be subject to sanctions. Venezuela has [the largest oil reserves](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u2zAMhZ9G3hTo386goYu227WjwSsxCQtZMmQ5hvP0hTv0BboQ30CQ5zu_vuYvoEzl-RMW9P1R54LHlrF3bPMbC352zFAq5Uc-qTwjtA3KrIRyXEguxjkB5XM2Q_IPRIV6QC9HN46Tvgs5vLyKVmtAcY_fVkoB8p5MslM0WumkrR3IX9eEFKOUwtjppu335AAcOFQupciMwES9ttvvSqW_8JHP-sZ2i3UZsn_1vm5M_2AqMBWO47jtG_Sa4LwWmApbr-1kKlxmTIW1ZuoUL7weMxWEvMZFve3Lyv9580qZF4o1w8YXSHurPGGOJ281NXru-GEqTJOwxkkjxMhUGJpP60E50-ZGZsRzAcp_o_b_6vft1Z8AAAD__ysEjds) in the world, but Chevron is the only major U.S. oil company still operating in the country after former Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez pushed to nationalize the country's oil industry.
## World's First Flying Car Enters Production
California-based Alef Aeronautics has [begun mass production](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDtuwzAQRE8jdTT4kUirYJHGndOmFChyKW-wXhoULcM5fWDnCKnnYQbzvs7zOSAhr5_hCr7lMjM8NoLWoM47MPzcgQIXpExP5DWGugWetdRWSCWkm1NAes5Dn3wG0GB68MpZ545mkqq_-FHFRUEc8mJ1NHqxyqicJzeNMBkVpx79q00q6ZSSw3g8mHE52hBssKBtSrEbJCRspR6-C3K7QKZn2aEeYrn25C-t3bbOfHT61OkTcoMKW0NegVdkgIq8vtB3yGUPDQt3-nTfRCDIAghiqxjF30MRQxW3WtI9vsC--nR7IBFu1nWDXK8B6b3c_qVr9_o3AAD__1fAglA) of its Model A, the world's first modern flying car that can drive on roads and take off vertically. Last year, the company released footage of the vehicle completing a test flight in San Mateo, rising from a closed roadway and flying over another car without external tethers. There is a lot of talk right now about immigration, and to be perfectly honest, it is exhausting.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3dd7533f-506b-4b5c-8ab2-dc90bbdecf4c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
What I know for certain is that most of the people having this conversation have never been immigrants, have never employed immigrants, and have never had to live under another country's immigration system. They are arguing from vibes, feelings, and slogans, not experience.
So I want to share mine.
I lived as an immigrant in China and Taiwan for more than a decade. When Americans, Europeans, or Australians do this, we like to use the word _expat_. That word is a lie. It is a class distinction meant to make people feel better about themselves.
I was an immigrant.
I lived six years in Beijing, seven years in Shanghai, two years in Taiwan, and spent time in Hong Kong. Some of that overlapped with finishing my undergraduate degree while bouncing between Hawaii and Beijing, but most of it was consecutive. China was home.
I went there for opportunity. I went there for quality of life. I should probably write an entirely separate piece on what quality of life actually means and why I eventually came back, because it is not what people imagine. Some of it is explained here:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/68e59d6d-57ba-47b0-bec6-5b8f24960351?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [I Criticize America Because I Chose It](https://substack.com/redirect/68e59d6d-57ba-47b0-bec6-5b8f24960351?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Jan 5
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/68e59d6d-57ba-47b0-bec6-5b8f24960351?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## How the System Actually Worked
While I was there, I worked in upper management in hospitality. I ran hotels, nightclubs, restaurants, and lounges, sometimes all under one roof. One venue on busy nights, we employed hundreds of people, with full-time staff in the triple digits.
The workforce was a mix of locals and foreigners. Some were fully documented. Some were not. Some were in gray areas that everyone understood but few spoke about directly.
This was not unique to one venue or one city. It was how the industry functioned.
That is not a moral defense. It is a description of reality.
* * *
## Everyone Knew the Rules
I have never entered a country without a visa. I have also lived in environments where it was widely understood that many people overstayed visas, worked outside their authorization, or existed in legal gray zones.
If you live inside immigrant communities abroad, this is not hidden. People know who is documented and who is not. Employers understand the risks. Governments understand what is happening.
Enforcement is selective, political, and often theatrical.
That does not make it right. It makes it predictable.
Early on, I observed how informal employment worked in sectors like education. Foreigners were hired because they were foreigners. Parents paid more for a foreign face speaking English. Schools paid cash. Everyone understood the arrangement.
The authorities understood it too.
China wanted growth. China wanted English literacy. China wanted foreign participation. So a blind eye was often turned.
Every so often, there would be visible enforcement. Immigration officials would show up. When that happened, schedules changed. People stayed home. Classrooms were rearranged. The director of our act said "action" for our preplanned choreography.
This was not chaos. It was theater.
* * *
## The "Wild West" Phase
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a66a5014-f9b4-4ba9-bca3-5886b2424cb4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
When I first arrived in China, it was still the tail end of what many foreigners referred to as the Wild West.
In certain foreign districts, visa services operated openly. Shell companies existed to sponsor foreigners. Documents were created, altered, or supplemented to fit requirements. If you wanted a visa, they would pull out a menu of visas to choose from. If you got in trouble and had enough money and connections, problems could often be "solved."
Eventually, China tightened the system. At the same time, it expanded formal visa pathways, especially for degree holders.
Many skilled workers still fell through the cracks. Chefs. Bartenders. Hospitality managers. Security professionals. People who were excellent at their jobs but did not meet formal credential requirements. So documents were forged for them. Diplomas were Photoshopped. Papers were submitted.
The result was not confusion. It was aligned incentives.
Everyone understood the risk. Everyone understood the game.
The rules were simple. Do not get caught.
* * *
## When Enforcement Came
I have personally experienced how unforgiving enforcement can be when it does arrive.
On one occasion, I had a valid visa that was deemed unacceptable because the visa was torn. There was no appeal process. No discussion. A decision was made, a phone call placed, and I was put on the next outbound flight.
The destination did not matter beyond whether I could enter that country without a pre-approved visa.
That is how I ended up in South Korea.
No one asked if I has a place to stay, if I could speak the language, if I even had any money for all of this, which I did (thank you student loans).
The priority was removal. Nothing else.
And there I was in Seoul.
* * *
## Raids Were Real
I have seen immigration raids in nightlife venues.
Immigration would storm the venue: 20 - 30 of them jumping out immigration vans.
Music cut. Lights up. Officers spreading out in the venue. Passports demanded.
Illegal employees blended into crowds. Changed out of uniforms. People disappeared into bathrooms or slipped out exits and ran for it.
If documents could not be produced, names were taken. Sometimes people were told to report later. Sometimes they were detained immediately.
I have seen people removed the same night.
There were no lawyers. No advocacy groups. No procedural theater.
If you were caught, you paid the fine, you were removed, and if you were fortunate, you were allowed to return months later.
Your family? They didn't care. Your school? Should have thought about that before. People were disappointed. But, nobody was shocked.
* * *
## These Were Not Tourists
This is another lie people tell themselves.
These were not just tourists trying to stay an extra three months.
These were students who had been in China four, six, eight years. People doing master's degrees. Doctorates. Medical residents working security at night. People who grew up in the Chinese school system from their teenage years. People with spouses. People with kids. People who had lived there for decades. They were good people.
They were also knowingly breaking the law.
Those things are not mutually exclusive. Complicity Was Everywhere.
Employers were complicit. Officials were complicit. Police were complicit. Communities were complicit. Foreigners were complicit. Everyone knew the rules.
We knew when immigration was coming. Sometimes the warnings were real. Sometimes they were wrong. Sometimes plans changed. But when the call came, people disappeared from their posts, blended into the crowd, or stayed home.
If they got caught, the business paid a fine and they got deported. That is how the system worked. The guilt was broad. The responsibility, however, always landed on the individual when enforcement came.
* * *
## Why I Am Telling This Story
I am telling this because American immigration discourse is usually built on regurgitated narratives and no experience.
One side pretends laws do not matter if intentions are good.
The other pretends the enforcement is clean, moral, and orderly.
Both are lying.
Immigration systems are messy. They are driven by labor demand, selective enforcement, incentives, corruption, and politics. People understand the rules. They make choices. Sometimes they succeed. Sometimes they lose.
I have seen people thrive for years. I have seen people lose everything overnight.
The one thing I never saw was surprise.
Everyone knew their role. And damn did I see some Oscar winning performances.
* * *
## A Necessary Clarification About America Today
Nothing in this is an endorsement of current ICE practices in the United States.
It is not an endorsement of masked agents, detaining Americans, or the stories circulating right now about abuse or overreach.
This is not a defense of cruelty.
This is not a call for authoritarian policing.
This is not a justification for lawlessness.
This is simply my lived experience as an immigrant under a different system, offered to puncture the fairy tales dominating this conversation.
We cannot fix what we refuse to describe honestly.
Disagree with me if you want. Argue with me if you want.
But stop pretending immigration is simple, clean, or morally pure on either side.

| \-- Reporting from the Political Front --
---
---
| | January 7, 2026
Following the last couple CT election cycles, realists here in the Conservative camp knew that to energize the CT GOP, the baton had to be passed to the burgeoning Gen-Z and Millennial generations. There were hopeful signs coming from the Gen-Zs, because they have come to age in the utter failure of hegemonic Democrat rule here in Connecticut. In the '24 and '25 cycles, several of them came out to work in a couple select campaigns, including my own run in '24.
These bleeding-edge Gen-Zs assured us there were many like them waiting in the wings. As they surfaced, to a one, they knew the fateful difference between Capitalism and Socialism - between Liberty and Collectivism, and what had to be done about it. Yes, the lessons too many of today's youth tragically never seem to have learned. We wholeheartedly encouraged their efforts to organize, providing our best 'dutch-uncle' advice.
Well - organize and emerge they did, and their efforts produced their dynamic group, [American Destiny](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKflh9UfX2IoRPAxgk0aIrdZHrRltHNUs8YlGmMMEQ5qRSvHMIvC5_U2DOWt-2fMHoR-ImanM--Y0IuXFs4Gb9w62Q==&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==) (www.AmDest.org). Their genesis is here in Connecticut, but they have taken their message and organizing skills out to their respective colleges and universities in those many different states, to strong effect. We wrote about their organizing and goals last fall in this Connecticut Centinal [Article](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKflyhhhgJT8gMOzgrBtSl8uW-YR72J6KKhdiiPHjJbJ-tsnJPbjiDo19d2B7DZnYYcW4NyMX04Ug8oRvcF8SF6u_7a3ecuoBJ6iKJ_wJaOr7pttnGZNgur76m6Cs8vpBdXFEHFNeDhaZhz1b8befuqYt8JO-a09YPcd_6wBJfZ_8UvKq2JVJGhso-QvY8roBPeVKT3nkjcTo_ZbobZfew_NkPGS67lGEhKNP1CrE_Z1DUE9erO5nTCnUA==&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==). They are action-oriented and aim to help restore our great Republic through the electoral process.
Their first commitment was demonstrated on Monday night in Stamford, with an endorsement event for Ryan Fazio's campaign for CT governor. The event was covered by The Connecticut Centinal, which published an [Article](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKfl99hBwJUpnU_kKWBGqcRyd4wrZcWQB4EzO4Q6yHgHjWDv98XEeOHxUHq4-Wfi5qQmiFvuS4Bxu0gg6wk_XUZeW8YyL7CZhopcXD0khx7uRnD2QIxC3PlkStTHZ3VVM9Dy3UCpkMj-U_CpbvPI5KWXvsGDh3yCORlY7iiBwXxTtIT-OTJXtAatELVtR_e1oioeMizDpj-26VqctA07FgVzbQW535NPjIEj&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==) last night and can be seen below. If you want to see these great youth have the positive impact we know they can, they'd appreciate anything you can contribute to their efforts: [Donate Here](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKflx-bPF5OT13fASWxgmE0vNHL1Z4xUOPjnkvcXuDpRLtlAkNQUoPijRvqf3bXxFSe6aGyQdqu1yaY-AYG4WTRY5S4kiXIyrSwaIYNRMN15ww8=&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==).

Conservative Youth Group Endorses Ryan Fazio for Governor Connecticut Centinal Staff
Below - Ryan Fazio (center) with some of the CT youth attending the American Destiny Endorsement event.
---
|
---
[American Destiny](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKfl6FrdeV5RIb87tjkM_Ei7doJ6f0f75cyahdoZmRABp0UdXcMIJjeJ4JRVY1S76uoOc8LpvrkQptoJnEJwWFzddthR2iKVDX0WnOTOT5wISHI=&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==) (AmDest), a youth-centered 501(c)4 [started](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKflyhhhgJT8gMOzgrBtSl8uW-YR72J6KKhdiiPHjJbJ-tsnJPbjiDo19d2B7DZnYYcW4NyMX04Ug8oRvcF8SF6u_7a3ecuoBJ6iKJ_wJaOr7pttnGZNgur76m6Cs8vpBdXFEHFNeDhaZhz1b8befuqYt8JO-a09YPcd_6wBJfZ_8UvKq2JVJGhso-QvY8roBPeVKT3nkjcTo_ZbobZfew_NkPGS67lGEhKNP1CrE_Z1DUHqszmSqgoJzw==&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==) by Connecticut high school and college students, endorsed Ryan Fazio for Governor at a packed event in Stamford on Monday night.
AmDest was launched in the past year by some very precocious Connecticut youth who got their feet wet in politics working for a couple Republican campaigns in the '24 cycle. They determined that a more action-oriented national group was needed - a complement of sorts to Turning Point's more educational focus. They position themselves as a 'force-multiplier' to political campaigns - to hit the ground with action, to do the nitty-gritty necessary to drive campaigns to victory. And they expect to do just that for Ryan Fazio's effort.
AmDest's [Paige Shepard](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKflFxG_-sLnPTCsg863urszReGzvpbhBgOolEkwYHxgmFxzfeKNM8P_F88b3WmUielEAYJRFq6I_n8VfF3NJ6O7s3NkNR5DQb7D1Qpu6A6wBarQHjvf9GHafr7BvnjDGVItSYG6K0wbg7di3-VvPkFrAF-f8MMjS1IbJDlBUWc6zVRNtsWUINY9M-j4rEt3Z_IvYdvmpiI2RbO3p25NdL4AFm3TfvVxc8kN&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==) emceed the night, first introducing [Chris Pettinella](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKflCmfB06--L-G2sg3pfhc6Pp8P5KLx4g9Zuzz2XzrOJjua4FJ0_SLlJaM7XCh0PBNr5dEUPFpLankj9PgHe83OJvrlWgbZz-deMTymf_di7yCV3JMdp2r9twQ4OpUL960Hbw_UiY0Rkw1_Gs531NmQiChvzn01bjhFkLVoLEFhpelj4v8oOfQgY4kPX-VsVwoue1Q1mwTCpHrgUthpuiDJExSzoEIKQU3PfaG1WL_KSJw=&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==), a recent Trumbull High School graduate and founder of The Edmund Burke Society at Trumbull High School. Pettinella, an inspiring young man, shared his experience running for office in Trumbull, knocking on nearly every door in town and even planting trees in potholes in what became a viral campaign moment. Unfortunately he lost, but he earned 300 more votes than the last person who ran for the seat, and he helped boost overall election day turnout.
His message was clear: Connecticut first matters, especially to young people.
He doesn't want to have to leave the state of Connecticut to have a decent life; he wants his future to be here. That's why he wants young people, including himself, to step up, engage in the political process, and help effect positive change.
Next up, [Blake Consentino](https://lk9rohfbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001XrfPSkSi6uK6WwdH0-3ZHdoWrIF1hg6cDFvJs5-uJ6j69WLmvom25VoIvjzkNKflwOunyabXj68a9L9tuIl7HFCuaDCyvGJ_tUUViSXJFpl7fCoALWyyR8wouKrfCABaqsnpqYvIclxy5VT3t1TxtwrJEO3bngbklw18Pv0LMry3L3Ckq2Yo5xISmChi2iQ7-fz8UVrbP0mtJXScOH9cBmen2U_LwMYsSzzEqsMVe8MCGzgY1BfO7_nXW2K7I_FdQXJYaOTZq7I=&c=GoWlHIAZzwDdyH5RVFf_YwhHRyhgxQ8QVx2Ffzt6-6aXABly8kvLnQ==&ch=Pla943hlPZ4BhLZ-uOaXmvOE0CH3RGXUTaumhomzR3cZnN-qrUKt_Q==), the founder and president of AmDest and a Connecticut First guy, started off his remarks by offering a "complete and unwavering endorsement" of Ryan Fazio for governor of Connecticut. "I can tell you with certainty that Ryan Fazio is our guy," said Consentino, a young man who clearly has a political future ahead of him.
"When has the status quo ever changed history? It has always been the visionaries, the dreamers, and the young. Those who are on the outside, because it is we who know a better world is possible," asserted Consentino. "We know a better state is possible. We must assert that, yes, we are here, and that we will no longer let what is ours be taken from us in the same vein."
"We are being systematically forced out of the very towns, cities, and neighborhoods where we grew up, the places where we were told we could one day live," he explained. "The world we were promised no longer exists. We can't afford to lose our inheritance. The time is late, but the time is now."
"Gen Z are choosing to fight. We will not give up on Connecticut. We will not retreat across state borders. We're not going to be silenced by our peers or professors by our government or other sensors. We will not have our roots ripped out from underneath us," he assured everyone.
"And we will do whatever it takes over the next 11 months to ensure that we win."
The young people in the room were very taken with the 35-year-old Fazio, who spoke to their concerns about affordability, open borders, home ownership, zoning control and more.
"As Governor, I will cut electric rates by 20 percent and make Connecticut affordable for all. I'll deliver a $1,500 income tax cut for the average family in Connecticut," said Fazio. "I will ensure that we have affordability for housing in our state while protecting local control, protecting our taxpayers and our families and our towns on a local level rather than giving free rein to developers to do whatever they want to turn Ridgefield into Rochester, Brooklyn, Connecticut, into Brooklyn, New York."
He also promised to reverse the Trust Act that makes Connecticut a sanctuary for illegals.
Fazio knows as well as American Destiny that people in Connecticut are hungry for a change, and they don't want to have to leave the state because of failed Democrat policies.
"Political leadership in this state has failed our residents worse than any other state in the country," said Fazio. "But I'm more optimistic than I've ever been."
Not just Fazio, but the whole room was brimming with hope - hope that in this election cycle Connecticut's patriotic youth will finally make the difference necessary to recapture the statehouse.

## Baby Box Used for First Time in Texas
A mother [surrendered her infant](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OwyAQRk9jd1gw_iEpKLZJl223tAY8tlEwRID_br9ytDfYej49vTc_z_6J1lk_feNCKh9j6D3tyVHOFPtMByYfBE5ovQm7DmcabSTqgUPHuGBc9gNad_ZNOSjNh7soSQnZSXmT0MpyVtQB1TiYWhjZQQujuGPTCA7tjRtTi9KqC8YFlwI4b6ESsjOtbkFLIW6mhqLhNNgcYpVn-iiN7gwbxcqEpXRqzvmdivqrgEcBj33fK9oonnm2fnKr1sG8rmUBjyvtmmA2M_s7sSuIRUpmJbbgixJD78PqDS3kM0Md1swSjsRm3MgzjfpkOhx0ocqohvdunbOpk0XDpwWt-3jl_31zU_AbAAD__3FLi9Y) at a Safe Haven Baby Box in Lubbock, marking the first time one of the devices has been used in Texas, officials announced Monday. Since revisions to the state's long-standing [Baby Moses law](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1uxCAUhE-Du0Xw1hhvQZHG3aZNifh5tpGwsYAs69tHcZELpB2NZj59X0_9NCGGffk0G6r6npPesZWItWLWFd-m7ImbxYTdpWbTWeaQETUwGG6M35jU3oR46r7zyjL_4B0qLgcpRwlCdqsaOQi0PRvvMFsLo-kfg-VcCGll78TQBfU7xjiTHBgTQLkcnLACrOR8dHcgPUMfasq0rnghzfFML8zUpa2Laq31KOT-QWAiMLXWqJ-PQq8mXdKLwOTWEL0-cqroakj7X1TMjPUkMGUs6Ts7LAQma-ypt1SwUFOOLit_tBBjKIMkPVs2E-J1Xf8n7KXgJwAA___NK4D6) went into effect in 2023, [more than a dozen](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOqzAQgOHTQAcaTwxDChevSZfXbonG9hC8cjCyLRJuv9pcYS_w6df_dZ_vHGLYHv_5Kaa-lzRv8ipRapU8V3lz2ZLiB4fNpZdNZ1lCFpkRcOxAdUCz5xDPWbfeWPBX1YpRNBJNhAO1q6Erg9Z81ejJTYsHC2wdjKPWFzdpbIP5xUABKQQYsFc0usEOaEmpyV2w0SA-1JT7usonaYlnOiT3Lj3baNZa99Jc_jV4a_C25_QtrnaFF-lWPmTrLNvTpnd_SHYSe973Bm9tNn5_hRhDGanR8HhyiB-x_u3DYfAnAAD__03ecZk) Safe Haven Baby Boxes have been installed at fire stations and hospitals throughout Texas. The law allows parents in crisis to surrender unharmed infants less than 60 days old legally and anonymously. The child was recovered from the box in [less than a minute](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu5CAMRb-GdIyMJ4FMQbEN3dt2ywiIM0HLwBMwyeTvV4n2D15j2ZLte-798zV92RBDev62L9Lts-Qp0V4jtUZlavSxNWVhnzYkn3eXj7qEQjQhoOQgOKhptiEeU9_N2sH8EB1poaRSo8JBdat2FmcYvQSBywjyIawdpe-lXPoHeuq7oM9nIEAJBBjwJpT0gxvQKSFGf0fWA82h5XJrK11ISzzyRuXm86uLem3tu7L7L4aGodn3_RbfzmX_N6cYEp1bDE1tuRwMzWnvGm0jhubUZmhAnOXs_t_ySlT5EkptnDYqvNqF-Go3StxZd3CXP7y-S6E0U-Eh8YuMoRlHuMseBIBiaLqi5-89xBiqVKyH58uGeIG3n8W9afwXAAD__yCqkjs), according to Lubbock Fire Rescue Chief Richard Stewart. "_I don’t know your situation or pain, but I do know in your darkest moment, you had the courage and love for your baby to give them an opportunity at life_ ," Stewart said. Monica Kelsey, CEO of Safe Haven Baby Box, also thanked the mother. "_Your baby is safe, and your baby is healthy, and the process is working for a forever family to get the call that they've been waiting for many years, probably_."

name: Doug Lloyd for MI Attorney General
subject: ICYMI: What Michigan Law Requires of Its Attorney General
body:
The Law Is Clear. The Experience Matters.
| | |
---
| | [](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019hEI7YLO7CesxCY-4rdsOPnkH3Xh6iz6ZNkVv4xpSJNhG78Yce6-0EcZzaKkCd_TWoYyD3KM08unNO8o7HKe5qnCD0u_gUYDnLuPK_hokVImAij_PuXVEKF4-19ZBQRzUnvhyoag2RypEEKWSM1pivyzqPhx3GfhFdv88IcKwFU=&c=nmZKKV7dQijPk_PB73019ku1HhkpC2lwEYROVSPsmA-eJgNqL_bMyg==&ch=CKCnw5meNguWgeJOEGzeJFgvpRPk6J_ko9LVuxepuVRZLkL4PgE4Nw==)
---
| | | [](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019hEI7YLO7CesxCY-4rdsOPnkH3Xh6iz6ZNkVv4xpSJNhG78Yce6-0EcZzaKkCd_TWoYyD3KM08unNO8o7HKe5qnCD0u_gUYDnLuPK_hokVImAij_PuXVEKF4-19ZBQRzUnvhyoag2RypEEKWSM1pitlxCcCXGlwq8rh-87vEk5Q=&c=nmZKKV7dQijPk_PB73019ku1HhkpC2lwEYROVSPsmA-eJgNqL_bMyg==&ch=CKCnw5meNguWgeJOEGzeJFgvpRPk6J_ko9LVuxepuVRZLkL4PgE4Nw==)
---
| | Friends,
As we begin the new year, I want to start with something that too often gets overlooked: what Michigan law actually requires of its Attorney General.
[Michigan Compiled Laws, Chapter 14, Section 30](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019hEI7YLO7CesxCY-4rdsOPnkH3Xh6iz6ZNkVv4xpSJNhG78Yce6-0AU7jC3ykCX4BKmEy7Tq8XJoRocFOIjnTanwWcuRGyJYLzfrtaKadgVK30ghiBqRVSnFl0ZRVHqm5JsDNxIGpyVmaTJ0LJLSWCZwihBGvzaIXl8o8wH0XGoZQWxH0NGZZsxbwGqh5vPILQpurk0xxUh4tWFqFy2vJnx2lZdo7CVEPObWjYy1GKY4NkrfbKpGsD_F2BQxTLcuKjqZy_TVAqtPIpmpaI52M5KhFY1KpPI3Qj8XBhli7KzIp7rQLbxCwapXJfdZOK4IhPbrxrc9m_BphmItRRY8Ppu60togcXbXiZr4h-0ysQgmXPD-WJEKM8XMDIEbaj4d&c=nmZKKV7dQijPk_PB73019ku1HhkpC2lwEYROVSPsmA-eJgNqL_bMyg==&ch=CKCnw5meNguWgeJOEGzeJFgvpRPk6J_ko9LVuxepuVRZLkL4PgE4Nw==) states plainly that the Attorney General shall "supervise the work of, consult and advise the prosecuting attorneys" across our state, and report that work to the Legislature.
In short, the Attorney General is not meant to operate in isolation. The office exists to support, guide, and strengthen local county prosecutors and, through them, uphold the rule of law in every Michigan community.
That raises a simple but important question: who is best prepared to do that job?
I believe the answer is someone who understands prosecution from every angle. Someone who has spent decades inside the system, not learning on the job. My background includes more than four years practicing real estate and business law alongside criminal defense, nearly 30 years serving at every level of a prosecutor's office, and over a decade as an elected public official accountable directly to the people.
I have spoken before about the support of 60 of my fellow elected prosecutors. That support matters not because I am an elected prosecutor myself, but because experience matters. On the other side of this race, there are two Democratic elected prosecutors, along with a former U.S. Attorney. All of them entered the race months before I did and had ample time to earn that same backing.
They did not.
The reason is simple. [The 60 prosecutors, more than 30 sheriffs, and dozens of retired judges, prosecutors, and law enforcement leaders supporting this campaign](https://jrhsf9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0019hEI7YLO7CesxCY-4rdsOPnkH3Xh6iz6ZNkVv4xpSJNhG78Yce6-0Pu6JfyMrrV6uQgsEy8fbAb5rUPz8Ba9Yoy8AlDpSLzV54BA0Zif0nCP1UAm75eqIwhoT4-JPHNmDiIX8ENIxBH7GKC_Y8Dv6yxIYCGEUhHrtqC9pVz20qONHTpqZOl5pQ==&c=nmZKKV7dQijPk_PB73019ku1HhkpC2lwEYROVSPsmA-eJgNqL_bMyg==&ch=CKCnw5meNguWgeJOEGzeJFgvpRPk6J_ko9LVuxepuVRZLkL4PgE4Nw==) do so because they understand what this job requires, and they know I have the experience, values, and steady leadership Michigan needs to fix what has gone wrong in the Attorney General's Office.
If, like me, you believe Michigan can do better, if you want to win in November and restore integrity, accountability, and the rule of law, I respectfully ask for your support at the Convention.
Because together, we can take Michigan back.

The Experience Matters. | | | | | == | | | == | | Friends, As we begin the new year, I want to start with something that too often gets overlooked: what Michigan law actually requires of its Attorney General. == states plainly that the Attorney General shall "supervise the work of, consult and advise the prosecuting attorneys" across our state, and report that work to the Legislature. In short, the Attorney General is not meant to operate in isolation. The office exists to support, guide, and strengthen local county prosecutors and, through them, uphold the rule of law in every Michigan community. That raises a simple but important question: who is best prepared to do that job? I believe the answer is someone who understands prosecution from every angle. Someone who has spent decades inside the system, not learning on the job. My background includes more than four years practicing real estate and business law alongside criminal defense, nearly 30 years serving at every level of a prosecutor's office, and over a decade as an elected public official accountable directly to the people. I have spoken before about the support of 60 of my fellow elected prosecutors. That support matters not because I am an elected prosecutor myself, but because experience matters. On the other side of this race, there are two Democratic elected prosecutors, along with a former U.S. Attorney. All of them entered the race months before I did and had ample time to earn that same backing. They did not. The reason is simple. == do so because they understand what this job requires, and they know I have the experience, values, and steady leadership Michigan needs to fix what has gone wrong in the Attorney General's Office. If, like me, you believe Michigan can do better, if you want to win in November and restore integrity, accountability, and the rule of law, I respectfully ask for your support at the Convention. Because together, we can take Michigan back. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | For the first time in the entire conflict - a coordinated strike on Russia's most protected facilities deep inside its territory. | Four strategic air bases. # **[1\. An independent path forward for Pennsylvania’s maverick senator](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=7ff4ff1a45&e=b7b3eddce2)**
_By Albert Eisenberg_ It’s 2026. America’s 250th birthday celebration is coming to Philly. The wheels have been hot-glued back onto the Eagles wagon. And our state’s senior U.S. Senator John Fetterman is more popular with Republicans than Democrats. There have been innumerable strange occurrences in the last decade in politics, but almost none more so than Fetterman’s transition from 2022[ _progressive darling_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=005c366e77&e=b7b3eddce2) to bane of America’s left wing. Whether in his obstinate refusal to appease Hamas and their growing number of supporters in the U.S., insistence that borders should exist and be enforced, or calling out Democratic intransigence on the government shutdown, Senator Fetterman has emerged as a voice of reason to many in Pennsylvania — and an apostate to the Democratic base. Polling[ _shows_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=81ac3641a9&e=b7b3eddce2) that Fetterman enjoys solid approval ratings overall, most significantly with Republicans (62-21 approve to disapprove), and floundering marks with Democrats. And he shows no signs of relenting; In an era where aesthetics and statements matter more than[ _actual votes_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=f6362cc57e&e=b7b3eddce2) (Fetterman sides with his Democratic colleagues much more often than not), there is no room for him to reassume the progressive posture demanded by activist Democrats. **Why It Matters.** Senator Fetterman is living through a social phenomenon that so many of us know too well: that Democrats demand ideological conformity, and exile dissenters. It is their _modus operandi_ for holding and maintaining power. Republicans, with all of our flaws, are just not like this. The Senator could make himself a happy home as a maverick Independent, and work his leverage within a grateful majority caucus — while giving himself an actual shot at winning reelection if he wants to run again in 2028. With his party base and legacy media moving against him, now is the best opportunity for Fetterman — and those who yearn for normalcy and moderation in politics — to make a change. [_Continue Reading_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=ceef8d33c7&e=b7b3eddce2)
---
|
---
|
# **2.**** [A New Year’s Resolution — Taking a count of the days left to me](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=dedf21ed39&e=b7b3eddce2)**
By Richard Koenig A friend of mine has urged me to think hard on the country song “Don’t Let The Old Man In.” He himself is bent on living out a full 100 years, and my bet is he’ll make it. Last year, in the space of eight months, he went big-game hunting in New Zealand, got a hip replacement upon return home to South Carolina, then set out on another expedition, this time to Colorado. If he’s to reach 100, he has 24 years to go. So do I. But I know this about me: The old man is already in, and he insists on telling me I might not have a lot of New Years ahead. I’m not complaining. I manage to swim a lot. It’s just that I don’t know that I can swim all the way to “triple digits,” to use a phrase you hear these days among my generation. What matters more is that I have yet to check off all the items on my to-do list, current and prospective, including a few big ones. So my resolution for the New Year is to give myself a little prod — actually, to firm up a practice I’ve let slip. Each week as I turn to the Monday page in my weekly planner, I’ll write there the number of days I have left to me should I die at a certain age short of 100. That number is arbitrary, fixed, and my secret. (My father died at 80, my mother at 97.) [_Continue Reading_](https://onpattison.us3.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a45553d37b628a10a8ae35af1&id=392967b6ab&e=b7b3eddce2)

---
|
