# [The 'Donroe Doctrine' Is Literally a Scam](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=183769470&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTgzNzY5NDcwLCJpYXQiOjE3Njc4MDU4MzQsImV4cCI6MTc3MDM5NzgzNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.pTgwiOCWXVJ07IdEermsVb9xsvc62vot8jZiUBl1BKg)
### It's not about pursuing U.S. interests--it's about using the U.S. government to pursue the private interests of Trump's oligarchic cronies.
| | [Aaron Regunberg](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)
---
| Jan 7
---
| [](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=183769470&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTgzNzY5NDcwLCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc2NzgwNTgzNCwiZXhwIjoxNzcwMzk3ODM0LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItNDk4MTE3MCIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.U_0azxNi1n2G48jmZNuTs9CAiqF1L31ZjChS7GYjVrc&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)
---
| | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=183769470&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&isFreemail=true&comments=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTgzNzY5NDcwLCJpYXQiOjE3Njc4MDU4MzQsImV4cCI6MTc3MDM5NzgzNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.pTgwiOCWXVJ07IdEermsVb9xsvc62vot8jZiUBl1BKg&r=1hvr60&utm_campaign=email-half-magic-comments&action=post-comment&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=183769470&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTgzNzY5NDcwLCJpYXQiOjE3Njc4MDU4MzQsImV4cCI6MTc3MDM5NzgzNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.pTgwiOCWXVJ07IdEermsVb9xsvc62vot8jZiUBl1BKg)
---
| | [](https://substack..T0Zo0akVqqGSZnW3GbUUQIQKBs3I5XGKDtRJTxnWZPw?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/aaronregunberg/p/the-donroe-doctrine-is-literally?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

It's been quite a busy few days for U.S. foreign policy. First was President Donald Trump's brazenly illegal abduction of Venezuela's head of state. Then Secretary of State Marco Rubio threatened to make good on his longtime dream of retaking Cuba, [warning](https://substack.com/redirect/6c9f0e23-4134-44df-8472-c3a862541fae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the Cuban government is "in a lot of trouble." And on Tuesday Trump's senior advisor on fascism (or whatever his title is) Stephen Miller [declared](https://substack.com/redirect/add2ab6f-d88c-4549-8193-9e5176b2a277?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Greenland belongs to the United States and that Trump could take the territory if he wanted. This "[Donroe Doctrine](https://substack.com/redirect/5ab8051d-87b9-4c71-a486-69dfd455592a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" as they've termed it, is based on a single principle: that, as Miller [ranted](https://substack.com/redirect/add2ab6f-d88c-4549-8193-9e5176b2a277?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the U.S. will henceforth "conduct ourselves as a superpower" by using our military "to secure our interests unapologetically in our hemisphere."
If you'd like to help unapologetically secure this newsletter's interests, please subscribe and recommend it to a friend!
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE4Mzc2OTQ3MCwicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc2NzgwNTgzNCwiZXhwIjoyMDgzMzgxODM0LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.QVPzRGeEl-tKMV6-fjjc_bIRsQr--puatrVMZgGWzF8?)
Here's the rub: When the Trump administration says "our interests," they're not talking about your or my interests, and they're not talking about the nation's interests. They're talking about the interests of corporate elites. **The Donroe Doctrine is a racket --nothing more and nothing less--designed to make the U.S. taxpayer underwrite resource imperialism for Trump and his billionaire buddies.**
They don't appear to be trying very hard to hide this reality. Trump has been pretty explicit that the Venezuelan takeover is not about freedom for Venezuelans. [Asked](https://substack.com/redirect/f5be1cc9-1c3f-4f80-9bc3-291a6c471588?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) whether he would demand the acting Venezuelan president offer amnesty to opposition figures or release political prisoners, Trump responded, "We haven't gotten to that. Right now, what we want to do is fix up the oil . . . ." The Venezuelan takeover is not about democracy. [Asked](https://substack.com/redirect/69496aea-1a43-4ffb-9943-9b13849cec22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) about plans for "free and fair elections," he responded, "Well, it depends . . . We're going to have to have big investments by the oil companies." According to Trump, kidnapping Maduro wasn't even about regime change. The new acting president of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, was vice president under Maduro, so the regime running Venezuela today is identical minus one person. When Trump was [asked](https://substack.com/redirect/f5be1cc9-1c3f-4f80-9bc3-291a6c471588?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "What do you need from Delcy Rodriguez?" His singular response: "Total access. We need access to the oil."
So this gunboat diplomacy is about oil. **But it 's not oil for American consumers.** The U.S. is already the largest oil producer in the history of the world, and no country on earth [exports](https://substack.com/redirect/c03a979e-6497-4353-be15-5f07fd60239b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more oil and refined oil products every day than we do. America's domestic gasoline sales have essentially [been flat for twenty years](https://substack.com/redirect/3363bdd9-d32c-4279-9e84-c31e7b1bc157?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), so the U.S. refineries in Texas and Louisiana [designed](https://substack.com/redirect/ed57dea2-cccd-40b7-bb50-ed878163bd02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to process Venezuela's expensive and dirty crude won't be increasing domestic supplies. Rather, they will convert that high sulfur oil into finished oil products for export out of the U.S., **which does** _**nothing**_**to lower prices at the pump for American consumers**.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/732d3510-6970-4882-a716-19cfc1570ebd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Trump's predatory assault would still be vile if moronic statements like this were true--but it's worth stressing that they absolutely are not.
So who does stand to gain from this takeover? The same people that all of this administration's policies are designed to benefit: Trump's billionaire buddies. In the case of Venezuela, these are the fossil fuel villains who are already poisoning our air and water and driving the increasingly catastrophic climate disasters that are destroying our homes, raising our property insurance rates, and threatening our future. That includes [corporations](https://substack.com/redirect/9a1e02ce-0d80-4d48-ab81-486d3512969d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) like ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips, which have used the controversial investor-state dispute settlement system to claim $15 billion and $30 from the Venezuelan government, respectively--claims Trump will likely use as a starting point for forced repayments to Big Oil. Both companies' stocks, as well as Chevron's, [jumped](https://substack.com/redirect/a6bed176-c241-4fe5-84a6-a13745b1aaa2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) following the Venezuela news on Monday.
Beneficiaries also include billionaires like Trump megadonor Paul Singer, whose hedge fund Elliott Management last November [acquired](https://substack.com/redirect/179d707a-d7e0-4ecb-9640-663d10936ef0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Citgo, the U.S.-based subsidiary of PVDSA, Venezuela's state-run oil company. Citgo's oil refineries stand to make huge profits from Venezuela's heavy crude oil reserves, according to the executive director of refining and oil products at the Oil Price Information Service (OPIS), who [called this access](https://substack.com/redirect/04862d6f-c765-46a9-ad0d-a0a43db7150c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) "a game changer for U.S. Gulf Coast and West Coast refiners in terms of profitability." Indeed, Trump has already launched that gravy train: On Tuesday he announced that Venezuela would be "turning over" 30 to 50 million barrels of oil--he [appeared](https://substack.com/redirect/d2741f62-9368-4977-9a0b-af45d168d47d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to be referring to stock built up during the U.S. blockade--to be sold at "market price" in the U.S. So refineries like those owned by Singer are about to be handed a massive windfall, while Trump--who took to social media to write "That money will be controlled by me, the President of the United States of America"--gets a new slush fund.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b5e8a986-e6e7-4c56-8e68-3a83b7d45f73?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It's wild how quickly Trump turned the U.S. into Putin's Russia. A kleptocracy, run by and for oligarchs, preying on our neighbors, funneling loot to our fascist leader.
In short, the Venezuelan takeover is, like most major endeavors across Trump's business and political career, a scam. The precise sequence of events leading him to target Venezuela and Maduro is anyone's guess--and doesn't really matter in the grand scheme of things. The outcome is the important thing: Trump plans to use your and my tax dollars to guarantee the profits of the fossil fuel billionaires who [bankrolled](https://substack.com/redirect/6e1c54af-07bd-4761-8374-baf93588261d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his campaign. Indeed, Trump just yesterday [confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/6523c50f-a0d2-494e-b5cf-9111057b5d67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that these companies should expect that "they'll get reimbursed by us"--while, of course, keeping every penny of the returns.
And we should expect the same approach to any future illegal landgrabs by this administration. Should the Trump team proceed with their unhinged plan to annex Greenland next, the [minerals](https://substack.com/redirect/0e57eaf0-9d8b-48c4-a80e-e0a56b4dc6ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [oil and gas reserves](https://substack.com/redirect/afbd37db-3d43-4357-8560-0e5b3049d25d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) buried there will not be safeguarded for our collective national welfare; they'll go to Trump's billionaire friends, to be exploited in the most profitable ways available to them.
That is the real Donroe Doctrine. **It 's not about pursuing U.S. interests--it's about using the power and resources of the U.S. government to pursue the private interests of Trump's oligarchic cronies.** Of course, the former is bad enough. Using one's military to, as Miller said, "secure our interests unapologetically in our hemisphere" is literally a description of the foreign policy of Mussolini and Hitler. But the Donroe Doctrine lacks even the fig leaf of supposedly doing all this for our shared national security and wealth.
The only good news is that there's real political vulnerability to this scam. Nobody likes getting ripped off, and voters don't want their tax dollars to finance the exploitation of other countries for the benefit of wealthy elites.
**But Democrats need to actually say this.** They need to explain why this rewarmed fascist nonsense is a terrible deal for the American taxpayers who'll be subsidizing those billionaire profits.
Not everyone has gotten the memo on this point. [Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer](https://substack.com/redirect/3c31a8d8-fc7a-483c-a0e5-68615ad3d82f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries](https://substack.com/redirect/4fb5e925-798c-427f-9de2-055c280a916d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the two most senior Democrats in the country, responded to Trump's attack on Venezuela first by excoriating Maduro--which only serves to frame his ouster as a positive achievement--and then by complaining about how Trump did not consult Congress prior to taking military action. This is political malpractice. Maduro being a bad actor is irrelevant to this debate for multiple reasons, including that his entire regime is still in place. And nobody cares all that much about dry proceduralism.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/900193b1-39b3-45ba-a734-9a42502ce4a8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is--and I really cannot stress this enough--_not_ an effective response to a blatantly kleptocratic fascist attack on another country.
It's looking increasingly unlikely, this week, that Venezuela will be the final target of Trump's imperial racketeering. So Democrats need to adopt a better message, fast. The Donroe Doctrine is a racket designed to cloak the greed of a small number of billionaires in the mantle of patriotic nationalism so that their profits can be insured by the public. Trump is putting up our treasure--and in the future, perhaps, our blood--to make the richest people in the world even richer, all while he continues to jack up our health insurance rates and cut programs that support working people. It's evil, it's toxic, and it's Democrats' job to make sure the American people understand that.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a25139cc-5649-4a06-a852-07ee407eacc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This essay appeared in _[The New Republic](https://substack.com/redirect/31d3326d-582f-43bc-87db-642fb3a33afa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , an excellent outlet.
Thanks for reading. If you liked this piece, please consider sharing it with a friend!

clean_body: It's not about pursuing U.S. interests--it's about using the U.S. government to pursue the private interests of Trump's oligarchic cronies. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more It's not about pursuing U.S. interests--it's about using the U.S. government to pursue the private interests of Trump's oligarchic cronies. | | | Jan 7 | | | | | | | | | | | | It's been quite a busy few days for U.S. foreign policy. First was President Donald Trump's brazenly illegal abduction of Venezuela's head of state. Then Secretary of State Marco Rubio threatened to make good on his longtime dream of retaking Cuba, that the Cuban government is "in a lot of trouble." And on Tuesday Trump's senior advisor on fascism (or whatever his title is) Stephen Miller that Greenland belongs to the United States and that Trump could take the territory if he wanted. This "" as they've termed it, is based on a single principle: that, as Miller , the U.S. will henceforth "conduct ourselves as a superpower" by using our military "to secure our interests unapologetically in our hemisphere." If you'd like to help unapologetically secure this newsletter's interests, please subscribe and recommend it to a friend! ? Here's the rub: When the Trump administration says "our interests," they're not talking about your or my interests, and they're not talking about the nation's interests. They're talking about the interests of corporate elites. The Donroe Doctrine is a racket --nothing more and nothing less--designed to make the U.S. taxpayer underwrite resource imperialism for Trump and his billionaire buddies. They don't appear to be trying very hard to hide this reality. Trump has been pretty explicit that the Venezuelan takeover is not about freedom for Venezuelans. whether he would demand the acting Venezuelan president offer amnesty to opposition figures or release political prisoners, Trump responded, "We haven't gotten to that. Right now, what we want to do is fix up the oil . . . ." The Venezuelan takeover is not about democracy. about plans for "free and fair elections," he responded, "Well, it depends . . . We're going to have to have big investments by the oil companies." According to Trump, kidnapping Maduro wasn't even about regime change. The new acting president of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, was vice president under Maduro, so the regime running Venezuela today is identical minus one person. When Trump was , "What do you need from Delcy Rodriguez?" His singular response: "Total access. We need access to the oil." So this gunboat diplomacy is about oil. But it 's not oil for American consumers. The U.S. is already the largest oil producer in the history of the world, and no country on earth more oil and refined oil products every day than we do. America's domestic gasoline sales have essentially , so the U.S. refineries in Texas and Louisiana to process Venezuela's expensive and dirty crude won't be increasing domestic supplies. Rather, they will convert that high sulfur oil into finished oil products for export out of the U.S., which does nothingto lower prices at the pump for American consumers. | | ---|---|--- Trump's predatory assault would still be vile if moronic statements like this were true--but it's worth stressing that they absolutely are not. So who does stand to gain from this takeover? The same people that all of this administration's policies are designed to benefit: Trump's billionaire buddies. In the case of Venezuela, these are the fossil fuel villains who are already poisoning our air and water and driving the increasingly catastrophic climate disasters that are destroying our homes, raising our property insurance rates, and threatening our future. That includes like ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips, which have used the controversial investor-state dispute settlement system to claim $15 billion and $30 from the Venezuelan government, respectively--claims Trump will likely use as a starting point for forced repayments to Big Oil. Both companies' stocks, as well as Chevron's, following the Venezuela news on Monday. Beneficiaries also include billionaires like Trump megadonor Paul Singer, whose hedge fund Elliott Management last November Citgo, the U.S.-based subsidiary of PVDSA, Venezuela's state-run oil company. Citgo's oil refineries stand to make huge profits from Venezuela's heavy crude oil reserves, according to the executive director of refining and oil products at the Oil Price Information Service (OPIS), who "a game changer for U.S. Gulf Coast and West Coast refiners in terms of profitability." Indeed, Trump has already launched that gravy train: On Tuesday he announced that Venezuela would be "turning over" 30 to 50 million barrels of oil--he to be referring to stock built up during the U.S. blockade--to be sold at "market price" in the U.S. So refineries like those owned by Singer are about to be handed a massive windfall, while Trump--who took to social media to write "That money will be controlled by me, the President of the United States of America"--gets a new slush fund. | | ---|---|--- It's wild how quickly Trump turned the U.S. into Putin's Russia. A kleptocracy, run by and for oligarchs, preying on our neighbors, funneling loot to our fascist leader. In short, the Venezuelan takeover is, like most major endeavors across Trump's business and political career, a scam. The precise sequence of events leading him to target Venezuela and Maduro is anyone's guess--and doesn't really matter in the grand scheme of things. The outcome is the important thing: Trump plans to use your and my tax dollars to guarantee the profits of the fossil fuel billionaires who his campaign. Indeed, Trump just yesterday that these companies should expect that "they'll get reimbursed by us"--while, of course, keeping every penny of the returns. And we should expect the same approach to any future illegal landgrabs by this administration. Should the Trump team proceed with their unhinged plan to annex Greenland next, the and buried there will not be safeguarded for our collective national welfare; they'll go to Trump's billionaire friends, to be exploited in the most profitable ways available to them. That is the real Donroe Doctrine. It 's not about pursuing U.S. interests--it's about using the power and resources of the U.S. government to pursue the private interests of Trump's oligarchic cronies. Of course, the former is bad enough. Using one's military to, as Miller said, "secure our interests unapologetically in our hemisphere" is literally a description of the foreign policy of Mussolini and Hitler. But the Donroe Doctrine lacks even the fig leaf of supposedly doing all this for our shared national security and wealth. The only good news is that there's real political vulnerability to this scam. Nobody likes getting ripped off, and voters don't want their tax dollars to finance the exploitation of other countries for the benefit of wealthy elites. But Democrats need to actually say this. They need to explain why this rewarmed fascist nonsense is a terrible deal for the American taxpayers who'll be subsidizing those billionaire profits. Not everyone has gotten the memo on this point. and , the two most senior Democrats in the country, responded to Trump's attack on Venezuela first by excoriating Maduro--which only serves to frame his ouster as a positive achievement--and then by complaining about how Trump did not consult Congress prior to taking military action. This is political malpractice. Maduro being a bad actor is irrelevant to this debate for multiple reasons, including that his entire regime is still in place. And nobody cares all that much about dry proceduralism. | | ---|---|--- This is--and I really cannot stress this enough--not an effective response to a blatantly kleptocratic fascist attack on another country. It's looking increasingly unlikely, this week, that Venezuela will be the final target of Trump's imperial racketeering. So Democrats need to adopt a better message, fast. The Donroe Doctrine is a racket designed to cloak the greed of a small number of billionaires in the mantle of patriotic nationalism so that their profits can be insured by the public. Trump is putting up our treasure--and in the future, perhaps, our blood--to make the richest people in the world even richer, all while he continues to jack up our health insurance rates and cut programs that support working people. It's evil, it's toxic, and it's Democrats' job to make sure the American people understand that. | | ---|---|--- This essay appeared in , an excellent outlet. Thanks for reading. When billionaires and corporations flood a campaign with cash, they’re not
doing it out of kindness. They’re making an investment — and they expect a
return.

That’s why, while healthcare costs skyrocket, politicians say their hands
are tied. Yet there’s somehow always money for corporate tax breaks.

corporate-backed crony in Washington answering to billionaires instead of
working people.

richest country in the world.

It wasn't about politics... or elections... or even about the culture war. His final book was deeply personal, and unlike anything Charlie had written before... It was about the Sabbath. About sacred rest. Reconnecting with God. Charlie wrote this book because he knew what America was missing... and what he nearly lost himself. He found that in a world addicted to busyness, noise, and scrolling... The most radical act of resistance is to STOP. To rest. To reflect. To return to God. This book is his blueprint for how we do that -- as individuals, as families, and as a nation. 🔥 You'll discover how Charlie learned to honor the Sabbath in a culture that never stops 🔥 How setting aside just one day a week gave him clarity, peace, and strength 🔥 Why he believed this message could spark a spiritual revival across America I know he would've wanted you to have this book. When you give today to Turning Point USA, you 're not just supporting the movement Charlie built -- you're helping pass on the message he felt most urgently in his final months. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

In 2024, I became the first Black woman ever elected to represent our state in Congress when I flipped one of the most competitive seats in the entire country from red to blue. That win didn’t happen by accident. It happened because Emerge invests deeply, strategically, and intentionally in women who are ready to lead with signature programs like Seated Together. | = Seated Together is Emerge’s advanced leadership program designed specifically to address the barriers Black women face when running for higher office. When I joined Seated Together, I got the training, clarity, and support network I needed — a group of Black women candidates who helped me sharpen my message, become relentless in fundraising, and stay grounded in my “why.” And the results speak for themselves: Seated Together has produced three members of Congress. Every day in Congress, I see how urgently we need more women — especially Black women — in these rooms. My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like. name: Mark Kelly
subject: Do not be afraid. Do not be silent. Speak out.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
We all remember what happened five years ago yesterday.
#

Peter —
Hey Peter, it's Mark.
We all remember what happened five years ago yesterday. Donald Trump sent a mob to the Capitol to steal an election.
He had just lost, fair and square, and he didn’t like the result. So he decided he was going to try to silence the voices of 81 million people.
It was one of the darkest days in the history of our country, but we made it through.
Now he’s back, five years later, and it’s the same scheme. His Secretary of Defense, Pete Hegseth, is trying to silence me right now. He thinks he can make an example out of me, and intimidate others into staying quiet.
But here’s the thing: Americans really like freedom of speech. You sign an oath to defend it when you join the military. Trying to silence people into compliance is just about the most un-American thing you can do. Period.
There is nothing Trump or Hegseth or anybody in that administration can do to shut me up. I am going to keep fighting for our people, our democracy, and our Constitution.
We’re not going to let him win. Not a chance. So, five years on from January 6th, I want you to take this to heart: **Do not be afraid. Do not be silent. Speak out.**
We’re going to get through this the same way we did back then: together.

This is our toughest yet, and I need a huge team behind me.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-mek-em-mar25.qIyu4X&refcode=em260105-1-160&t=1&akid=4059%2E734936%2ES8-5cr) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $5](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1061?c0=ruben-mek-em-mar25.Savuis&refcode=em260105-1-160&t=20&akid=4059%2E734936%2ES8-5cr)**

My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like.

You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.

# Trump moves to secure Venezuela oil exports
President Donald Trump **[announced Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/8a0f5710-10db-4444-92ce-4b5154be975e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that the United States will take control of up to 50 million barrels of Venezuelan oil initially, with shipments to continue indefinitely following a U.S. military action that ousted Nicolas Maduro last weekend, as sanctions are selectively eased to reroute flows from China.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8a0f5710-10db-4444-92ce-4b5154be975e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Maduro ousted militarily:** U.S. forces removed Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in a raid last Saturday, paving the way for American oversight of the country's vast oil resources.
* **Sanctions selectively reduced:** U.S. will roll back targeted sanctions to allow global sales and transportation of Venezuelan crude, previously blocked under prior restrictions.
* **Proceeds U.S.-controlled:** Oil sale revenues will flow into accounts managed by the United States, with funds released back to Venezuela only at Washington's discretion to benefit both nations.
* **Oil rerouted from China:** Previously destined mostly for Chinese buyers, Venezuela's heavy crude will now ship directly to U.S. docks, boosting American access to OPEC founder's reserves.

# Venezuelan oil surge boosts US refiners
Analysts predict **[a full resumption of Venezuelan heavy crude exports](https://substack.com/redirect/0d972b0f-5b1f-4a04-83f2-2a06b7c08ff3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** could slash fuel production costs for American refiners on the Gulf Coast, who are poised to absorb up to 1 million barrels per day if sanctions are fully lifted.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0d972b0f-5b1f-4a04-83f2-2a06b7c08ff3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Gulf refineries gear up:** Gulf oil refineries were originally built to handle Venezuelan heavy sour crude oil, historically processing 800,000 barrels per day before 2019 sanctions, with current capacity for 3-4 million barrels per day of similar grades.
* **Chevron leads operations:** As the only U.S. major with a sanctions-exempt license, Chevron is currently importing 150,000 barrels per day while Valero, PBF Energy, and Phillips 66 stand ready to increase volumes.
* **Canadian producers hit:** Canada stands to be hit hardest by the competition, as cheaper Venezuelan barrels displace their heavy oil exports to U.S. markets, alongside higher costs for small Chinese refiners.
* **Rebuilding takes years:** Despite quick export redirection potential, it will require billions in investment to repair dilapidated infrastructure and ramp up production well beyond current levels.

# **" AI Fatigue" hits Wall Street hard**
Investors are showing signs of **["AI fatigue"](https://substack.com/redirect/e13e4714-41d4-4e38-9a05-5dc06f655207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after three years of hype-driven gains, shifting focus from the dominant Magnificent Seven tech giants to the S&P 500's other 493 stocks amid doubts over AI's promised economic payoff.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e13e4714-41d4-4e38-9a05-5dc06f655207?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Magnificent Seven Underperforms Recently** : Since late October, the group fell 2% while the rest of the S&P 500 rose 1.8%.
* **Ex-Mag Seven ETF Surges** : Defiance's XMAG saw inflows quadruple in December and gained 15% in 2025.
* **S &P 493 Margins Stay Strong**: Profit margins held elevated despite tariffs, efficiency drives, and labor weakness.
* **Cyclical Stocks Poised for Gains** : Improved economy could boost lenders like JPMorgan and consumer names like Nike.

### **AMD shares slide despite AI boom claims**
Advanced Micro Devices shares **[dropped as much as 4.4%](https://substack.com/redirect/aafc7395-3277-41e7-b01d-b76dae35f615?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Tuesday, erasing earlier gains, even as CEO Lisa Su touted soaring AI-driven demand for computing power and insisted the technology's widespread adoption in 2026 will prove it's far from hype.
* **CEO Highlights Massive Growth** : Su predicted computing power must increase 100-fold in the next four to five years, declaring "we are still in the early innings of unlocking the power of AI."
* **New Chip Targets Data Centers** : At CES, Su unveiled a new processor designed for corporate data centers while showcasing the top-tier MI455X AI accelerator.
* **Investor Skepticism Fuels Decline** : Shares slid amid concerns over a potential AI spending bubble after a 77% surge last year raised lofty expectations.
* **AMD Challenges Nvidia Dominance** : Positioned as Nvidia's top rival in AI chips, AMD outperformed its competitor in 2025 gains but saw shares fall while Nvidia's rose slightly.

# **SanDisk surges on Nvidia AI boost**
SanDisk Corp. shares **[soared 28% Tuesday](https://substack.com/redirect/a902b475-2fb0-4876-88fe-98abd944e67e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , the biggest gain since February, after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang touted massive untapped demand for storage as the "working memory" for global AI systems during his CES keynote.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a902b475-2fb0-4876-88fe-98abd944e67e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Huang highlights unserved market:** Nvidia's leader called storage a completely underserved sector poised to become the world's largest, holding AI's working memory.
* **Peers ride the wave:** Western Digital and Seagate posted double-digit gains, topping S&P 500 performers amid sector-wide momentum.
* **Memory prices climbing fast:** Reports indicate Samsung and SK Hynix seeking 60-70% hikes in server DRAM prices for Q1.
* **AI inferencing drives future** Analysts see storage firms as key beneficiaries of 2026 shift to AI at the edge in drones, vehicles and surveillance.

# Rhode Island targets wealthy amid Trump cuts
Rhode Island's Democratic governor is warming to a proposed **[3% income surtax](https://substack.com/redirect/411592d2-f033-4fe7-8515-c1ba03a6ce29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** on the state's top 1% of earners -- those making over $640,000 annually -- to plug a looming budget deficit worsened by anticipated federal cuts under President Trump to Medicaid and food assistance programs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/411592d2-f033-4fe7-8515-c1ba03a6ce29?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Governor Shifts Stance:** Dan McKee now supports the surtax if paired with tax relief for businesses, seniors and others, reversing his earlier opposition from last spring.
**Budget Pressures Mount:** The state faces at least a $101 million deficit for the upcoming fiscal year, potentially growing by another $70 million due to reduced federal funding and ongoing economic struggles.
**Massachusetts Model Inspires:** Lawmakers eye neighboring Massachusetts' 4% millionaire's tax, which has generated $6.2 billion in revenue since 2022, as a successful blueprint for addressing inequality.
**Additional Wealth Measures:** A separate "Taylor Swift tax" surtax on second homes valued over $1 million takes effect this summer, building on recent increases to gas, hotel and parking fees.

allies, and the billionaire class. Demand Justice pulls back the curtain —
naming names and showing exactly how these judges threaten our rights.

healthcare, abortion access, voting rights, worker protections. Your

subject: Let’s show Washington how we can fight like Michigan
body:
[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/685?t=1001&akid=3564%2E898137%2EVWCq3O ][IMG]

Team,

We make things. We build things. We imagine things that have never been
built before, then we go out there, we work our asses off. And we get it
done.

That’s my story. And that’s the story of Michigan.

Before I came to public service, I was an industrial designer — working on
everything from cars to well...toy cars (Hot Wheels, to be exact!). I loved
the experience of coming up with an idea, sketching it, drawing it out,
building models with my hands, and then when I saw it on the shelves, and
someone could go buy that thing that I made — that feels really damn good.

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-jan2026.Z4k7f1&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM1_V1_S1&t=1002&akid=3564%2E898137%2EVWCq3O ]Here's me in my college design studio with some concept sketches for
one of my car designs

Here's me in my college design studio with some concept sketches for one
of my car designs

Michiganders are united by the desire to build something that we're proud
of, something that's never been done before.

We have an opportunity in this next election to change the course of the
entire country. Michigan is one of a handful of states that the entire
country watches to see where we go next. So the future of 2028 depends on
what we do in Michigan in 2026. We have delivered here in Michigan as a
contrast to what's happening in Washington, which is very little.

When Michigan Democrats got power, we governed like we give a damn, and we
focused on families, on affordability, on jobs, and on education. We
focused on the things that matter to people, and now it’s time to show
Washington how we can fight like Michigan, how we can win, how we can
deliver, and how we can build our own future together.

[ https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/4?c0=mam-em-jan2026.Z4k7f1&refcode=AU_MAM_FR_GEN_GEN_AC_20260107_PM1_V1_S1&t=1003&akid=3564%2E898137%2EVWCq3O ]Are you with me? Let’s build something powerful, together. Donate to my
campaign for Senate today. It’s time to get to work and show the rest of
the country how Michigan gets it done.

name: Kate Rullo
subject: Volunteer Call To Action 1/7/26
body:
**_Hello and thank you for volunteering to share your talents with us!_**
**_
_**
**_This is the first of our weekly "Action Items" emails, designed to let our team know where they can get involved and help the campaign in the near future. I will also send a more general Campaign Update email once a month to ensure everyone is up to date on our progress._**
**_
_**
**_If you would prefer not to receive one or both of these emails, please reply to this message and I will update your preferences._**

Volunteer Needs: January 7–14, 2026

_Host a Meet and Greet Event_
Now that the holidays are over, we are ramping up our schedule of Meet and Greet events. These intimate gatherings allow a host to invite guests to meet Alan and generate excitement and fundraising support. We are hoping to schedule several such events in January and February. If you are interested in hosting a Meet and Greet or know someone who is, please email [Christina Proctor](mailto:christina@bradstockforcongress.com).

_Join the Social Media Team_
Our social media team is ready to get to work. We're looking for volunteers with a social media presence and savvy to assist in creating and sharing content around the campaign. Please email [Christina](mailto:christina@bradstockforcongress.com) or [Tesse](mailto:tesse@bradstockforcongres.com) if you are interested.

_Petition Collection_
To be included on the May 19th primary ballot, Pennsylvania congressional candidates must collect a minimum of 1,000 signatures. We are aiming for 2,000 signatures.

\- Circulation Period: February 17th through March 10th.
\- Need: We need volunteers in every county in the District to collect signatures from registered voters. Meet and Greets are an excellent way to collect signatures.
\- Training: We will hold a Petition Collection Training and Volunteer Orientation session on Thursday, January 22nd, via Zoom. A separate invitation with details will be sent to all volunteers.

Please help us reach people in your community. If you know of an event that's happening in your community that would be a good opportunity for Alan to speak to people (even those who may not typically vote Democrat), please send [me an email](mailto:kate@bradstockforcongress.com) and I'll see if we can make it work.

Thank you again for sharing your time and talent! Please feel free to contact me with any questions or ideas in the meantime.

Best,
Kate

\--

Kate Rullo
m: 412-996-0079

[DONATE HERE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/bradstock)

name: Mark Kelly
subject: They’re not going to shut me up
body:
You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.
Peter,
Pete Hegseth decided he's going to censure me, and is threatening to demote me and reduce my pension.
I got shot at in service to this country. I missed holidays and birthdays. I commanded a space shuttle mission and launched to the International Space Station while my wife recovered from a gunshot wound to the head.
My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like.
You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.
Pete Hegseth can threaten to reduce my rank and my pension. But I am not going to let him intimidate me, or anyone else. He is not going to stop me from defending our democracy from a president who is hellbent on destroying it.
If they think this is going to shut me up, they’ve got another thing coming.
**[And if you’re still with me, please: Split a donation between Wes Moore and me so we can fight back.](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260107-1.Zf9GSr&refcode=em-20260107-1&t=1&akid=1171%2E1086043%2EOB8pIP)**

Don’t give up the ship.
Mark

name: Mark Kelly
subject: They’re not going to shut me up
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.
| Team:

Pete Hegseth decided he's going to censure me, and is threatening to demote me and reduce my pension.

I got shot at in service to this country. I missed holidays and birthdays. I commanded a space shuttle mission and launched to the International Space Station while my wife recovered from a gunshot wound to the head.

My rank and retirement are things that I earned through my service and sacrifice for this country. Generations of servicemembers have done the same. Pete Hegseth wants to send a message to every single one that he will come after them if they say something he doesn’t like.

You swear an oath to the Constitution when you join the military — including the First Amendment right to free speech. We swore to defend the foundational principles of this country. I took that oath seriously 40 years ago, and I still do.

Pete Hegseth can threaten to reduce my rank and my pension. But I am not going to let him intimidate me, or anyone else. He is not going to stop me from defending our democracy from a president who is hellbent on destroying it.

If they think this is going to shut me up, they’ve got another thing coming.

**Farmers just want to be able to do their jobs, Peter.**

It's what Christina has heard over and over again when she talks to farmers across the district. And it's what she kept at the center of her talk about the need for a new Farm Bill last month at the Iowa Farmers Union convention. To her, this is personal:

Christina's dad grew up on the family farm. Throughout his childhood, it was always the family’s hope that one day he would take it over and keep the family legacy going. But it was a small farm, costs were high, profit margins were slim — and it didn’t help that the interstate took part of the property. In the end, they just couldn’t make a living. So her dad dropped out of school to work construction, and the rest is history.

Too many family farms in Iowa are at risk. Tariffs, big ag consolidation, and a lack of competition are driving up costs, while trade wars are taking away markets. And thanks to a dysfunctional Congress, we still don’t have a Farm Bill.

**Iowa’s farmers need real representation, not someone who pays lip service to them while failing them at every turn.**

Christina knows we all just want a chance to thrive and lay down the foundation for a good future for our families. And she is going to fight for that opportunity for each and every person in the district, including our farmers.

clean_body: | = Farmers just want to be able to do their jobs, Peter. It's what Christina has heard over and over again when she talks to farmers across the district. And it's what she kept at the center of her talk about the need for a new Farm Bill last month at the Iowa Farmers Union convention. To her, this is personal: Christina's dad grew up on the family farm. Throughout his childhood, it was always the family’s hope that one day he would take it over and keep the family legacy going. But it was a small farm, costs were high, profit margins were slim — and it didn’t help that the interstate took part of the property. In the end, they just couldn’t make a living. So her dad dropped out of school to work construction, and the rest is history. Too many family farms in Iowa are at risk. Tariffs, big ag consolidation, and a lack of competition are driving up costs, while trade wars are taking away markets. And thanks to a dysfunctional Congress, we still don’t have a Farm Bill. Iowa’s farmers need real representation, not someone who pays lip service to them while failing them at every turn. Christina knows we all just want a chance to thrive and lay down the foundation for a good future for our families. And she is going to fight for that opportunity for each and every person in the district, including our farmers. = Thank you, Team Bohannan Christina Bohannan is a mom, law professor, engineer and former state representative. She's running for Congress to defeat Mariannette Miller-Meeks and flip IA-01 blue. Look, being a former Republican isn’t my whole story.

My mother immigrated from the Philippines as an organic chemist. I followed in her footsteps and majored in biochemistry before I went to Law School to pursue my true passion – Constitutional Law.

**Looking back, the Constitution was my first love.** At 10, I was obsessed with the Watergate Scandal. _(Little did I know that was child's play compared to what Trump would do)_.

I know that sounds boring and nerdy, but the promise of our democracy, freedoms, and the rule of law fascinates me – and for years I _thought_ Republicans upheld those same ideals.

Trump does not have the power to go to war without congressional authorization, or to hand control of another country over to a cadre of oil companies. This illegal occupation could destabilize the region, set a dangerous precedent in the U.S., and embolden other countries to start their own wars of choice. The Trump Administration claims it targeted Maduro because of drug trafficking. But if Trump were serious about helping end the overdose crisis, he wouldn’t be kicking people off of Medicaid or defunding drug treatment and prevention programs. body:
The time is now to advance a BOLD conservative agenda to deliver on GOP promises made to the American people.
[](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.teapartypatriots.org/1/0100019b99f1e03b-7d764989-5904-41d4-87bf-350bb857eecc-000000/Ls1NVbhscnseQut_bAdyou94WFtjk8EutekBRsY07hA=439)Patriot–Act now—tell Republican leaders that we expect them to deliver results to protect our elections, enforce border security, cut federal spending, combat fraud, and hold unelected bureaucrats accountable.The House Freedom Caucus [_**issued a detailed “battle plan”**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.foxnews.com%2Fpolitics%2Fhouse-freedom-caucus-lays-out-gop-battle-plan-ahead-republicans-huddle-trump/1/0100019b99f1e03b-7d764989-5904-41d4-87bf-350bb857eecc-000000/XXdxnQhXp3gjJAWoPF-OMRNIhQTG2_evt6KoE9PDgyA=439) letter to Speaker Mike Johnson and the entire House Republican leadership ahead of a strategy meeting with President Trump, outlining conservative policy goals to guide GOP legislative efforts.[READ FREEDOM CAUCUS LETTER](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Fwww.foxnews.com%2Fpolitics%2Fhouse-freedom-caucus-lays-out-gop-battle-plan-ahead-republicans-huddle-trump/2/0100019b99f1e03b-7d764989-5904-41d4-87bf-350bb857eecc-000000/ZKplrIY7DRHMFc5dMjb-lIX5ydfmg7V61OzZofhgQWI=439)The Freedom Caucus agenda is a blueprint for reclaiming our national sovereignty and values, and we need your help to reinforce this message and let Republican leaders know we expect results on these policy priorities.We must safeguard our elections from non-U.S. citizens voting by passing the SAVE Act, limiting early voting, and reforming the census to only count American citizens. President Trump even fully endorsed The SAVE Act while speaking before the entire US House Republican conference this week, suggesting we should change the name to **The SAVE America Act** – because it is that important.[_**Tell Congress you expect them to slash federal spending, to eliminate fraud-plagued federal programs, punish states that enable fraud, and immediately deport any immigrants defrauding the American taxpayer.**_****](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Faction.teapartypatriots.org%2Fpetition%2Fits-time-to-deliver%2F/1/0100019b99f1e03b-7d764989-5904-41d4-87bf-350bb857eecc-000000/dtrTZvJwYUq8f74KOM71YoIrOnC-NiJxNlwifdNRRs8=439) Just look at what was uncovered in Minnesota this week that forced their radical governor and former VP candidate to Kamala Harris to drop his bid for re-election.[CALL CONGRESS](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Faction.teapartypatriots.org%2Fpetition%2Fits-time-to-deliver%2F/2/0100019b99f1e03b-7d764989-5904-41d4-87bf-350bb857eecc-000000/SzKeE2M-JjKHO63t5YmYkUh39AYZJpfpQmMxGgt6e3U=439)President Trump has successfully secured the border, but Congress must codify into law.It is time for Congress to be bold! Pass the American First agenda that the American people voted for and get rewarded in the upcoming midterms. The House Freedom Caucus has put forth a roadmap, all that Congress must do is follow it.
[_**Call your member of Congress today**_****](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Faction.teapartypatriots.org%2Fpetition%2Fits-time-to-deliver%2F/3/0100019b99f1e03b-7d764989-5904-41d4-87bf-350bb857eecc-000000/EGHVTcRJcLscOvt-gCgw0y-S33LUc_SiSOG-tOsx5c4=439) and tell them to adopt the House Freedom Caucus Blueprint!In liberty

name: Win Without War
subject: Venezuela
body:
The Trump administration bombed Venezuela this weekend.
#
**Donald Trump** rang in 2026 by bombing Venezuela’s capital, capturing its president, and announcing that the United States will “run” the country for the indefinite future to "get the oil flowing."
**There is NO congressional authorization for these strikes. This operation is illegal** , just as the earlier boat strikes off the Latin American coast were illegal. And yet, Trump is already threatening to rinse and repeat this horrible playbook in Colombia, Mexico, Cuba, and Greenland.
**Trump cannot rule the United States, nor any other country, like the king he imagines himself to be.** Venezuelans must have a say in their own futures, and people in the United States must mobilize to push Congress to take immediate action to rein in this lawless White House.
**[It’s up to us, the people, to make sure lawmakers feel enough heat from constituents to stop Trump from future escalation and violence. Click here to demand Congress pass a war powers resolution NOW.](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22146?source=em20260107-1441&t=13&akid=1441%2E2118727%2E1ScJpn)**
**[ACT NOW](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22146?source=em20260107-1441&t=14&akid=1441%2E2118727%2E1ScJpn)**
This operation was never about drugs or democracy. The simple truth is that Venezuela is not a major supplier of drugs to the United States. This was always about profit and power — and a would-be authoritarian hoping to distract the world from his falling approval rates and failing policies.
Much like Libya, Iraq, and Afghanistan before, deposing Maduro in Venezuela will hurt people, cause regional chaos, and solve nothing.**If Congress doesn’t rein Trump in, he will only be further emboldened to commit more lawless and unaccountable violence against anyone, anywhere.**
Venezuelans have endured years of repression and economic collapse. Some may feel relief at the chance for new leadership, while others fear the future. **One thing remains clear: Venezuela’s future should belong to its people, NOT Trump or U.S. oil companies.**
[**War powers resolutions already introduced in both chambers would throw crucial roadblocks on Trump’s path to being an unaccountable strongman — sign now to make sure passing them is Congress’s top priority.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22146?source=em20260107-1441&t=15&akid=1441%2E2118727%2E1ScJpn)
Thank you for working for peace,
The Win Without War team

**LeftNet is an online political network fighting for progressive causes and candidates focused on social, racial, economic, and environmental justice.**

Donald Trump rang in 2026 by bombing Venezuela’s capital, capturing its president, and announcing that the United States will “run” the country for the indefinite future to "get the oil flowing." There is NO congressional authorization for these strikes. This operation is illegal , just as the earlier boat strikes off the Latin American coast were illegal. And yet, Trump is already threatening to rinse and repeat this horrible playbook in Colombia, Mexico, Cuba, and Greenland. Trump cannot rule the United States, nor any other country, like the king he imagines himself to be. Venezuelans must have a say in their own futures, and people in the United States must mobilize to push Congress to take immediate action to rein in this lawless White House. This operation was never about drugs or democracy. The simple truth is that Venezuela is not a major supplier of drugs to the United States. This was always about profit and power — and a would-be authoritarian hoping to distract the world from his falling approval rates and failing policies. Much like Libya, Iraq, and Afghanistan before, deposing Maduro in Venezuela will hurt people, cause regional chaos, and solve nothing.If Congress doesn’t rein Trump in, he will only be further emboldened to commit more lawless and unaccountable violence against anyone, anywhere. Venezuelans have endured years of repression and economic collapse. Some may feel relief at the chance for new leadership, while others fear the future. One thing remains clear: Venezuela’s future should belong to its people, NOT Trump or U.S. oil companies. body:
Over the weekend, Donald Trump carried out an illegal and reckless military action in Venezuela without congressional authorization.
#
Over the weekend, Donald Trump carried out an illegal and reckless military action in Venezuela without congressional authorization.
At a moment when families are struggling with skyrocketing health care costs, unaffordable housing, and the everyday costs of groceries and prescription drugs, **Donald Trump wants to put American lives and taxpayer dollars on the line so his billionaire allies can profit off another country’s oil and minerals.**
**The American people don’t want another generation of forever wars. Neither do I.**
That’s why I voted last month in support of two War Powers Resolutions that would have prevented actions we saw this weekend and stopped further military escalation in the Caribbean. But ultimately, Republicans defeated the measures.
**As we head back into session this week, I’m pushing for new War Powers Resolutions to prevent further military action in Venezuela and to block the expansion of this dangerous pursuit of other countries’ natural resources.**
But the reality is this: as long as Republicans control the House, it will remain harder to stop this reckless escalation and hold Donald Trump accountable.
Taking back the House this year is essential if we want Congress to serve as a real check and refocus our government on lowering costs and improving people’s lives here at home.

Over the weekend, Donald Trump carried out an illegal and reckless military action in Venezuela without congressional authorization. At a moment when families are struggling with skyrocketing health care costs, unaffordable housing, and the everyday costs of groceries and prescription drugs, Donald Trump wants to put American lives and taxpayer dollars on the line so his billionaire allies can profit off another country’s oil and minerals. The American people don’t want another generation of forever wars. Neither do I. That’s why I voted last month in support of two War Powers Resolutions that would have prevented actions we saw this weekend and stopped further military escalation in the Caribbean. But ultimately, Republicans defeated the measures. As we head back into session this week, I’m pushing for new War Powers Resolutions to prevent further military action in Venezuela and to block the expansion of this dangerous pursuit of other countries’ natural resources. But the reality is this: as long as Republicans control the House, it will remain harder to stop this reckless escalation and hold Donald Trump accountable. Taking back the House this year is essential if we want Congress to serve as a real check and refocus our government on lowering costs and improving people’s lives here at home. In solidarity, Sarah McBride

Folks, it’s James Carville.
I’ve been around the block a few times and worked on a heck of a lot of campaigns. So believe me when I tell you: **This ain’t good.**
John Sununu — yeah, _those Sununus_ — just jumped into the U.S. Senate race in New Hampshire. And now the political eggheads have DOWNGRADED Democrats’ chances of winning there.
**[💥Before you read another word, split $10 or whatever you can between Chris Pappas and State Democrats Committee to help Chris fight back right now.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/99094?refcode=em20260107-9913&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=9913%2E614464%2E3rC-yl)**

This isn’t some back-bench, no-name guy we’re up against. **Sununu’s won a Senate seat before.**
He’s got name ID, deep pockets, and Wall Street’s dark money machine ready to drown us in attack ads. This is the far-right’s big play, y’all — they know if they take New Hampshire, Democrats have _no viable path_ to flipping the Senate.
Chris Pappas is the real deal. I mean it. He’s won the toughest district in New Hampshire four damn times, and he knows how to bring folks together. But he cannot — **_cannot_** — do this alone.
So here’s what I need from you:
**[Split a contribution between Chris Pappas and State Democrats Committee today. $10, $25, whatever you can spare. Because if we let the GOP buy this seat for Sununu, we’re gonna be stuck with Republican control for years to come.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/99094?refcode=em20260107-9913&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=9913%2E614464%2E3rC-yl)**

I’m mad as HELL that this race just shifted in the wrong direction — but that means it’s time to get serious. Chris is the only one who can hold this seat, but he needs a hell of a lot more firepower to fend off what’s coming.
Let’s show these Republican bigshots that we’re not scared — and we sure as hell ain’t backing down.
**[Give what you can right now.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/99094?refcode=em20260107-9913&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=5&akid=9913%2E614464%2E3rC-yl)** Let’s win this damn thing and flip control of the Senate.

Peter, **Yesterday marked five years since January 6 — the day a violent mob attacked the People’s House.** I stood on the House floor to say what needs to be said out loud, even when some folks would rather deny history. **No tweet. No post. No spin. No ugly, lie-filled website from the Trump admin can change what happened that day.** Brave Capitol Police officers were beaten while protecting our democracy. It requires clear objectives, congressional engagement, and a sober assessment of consequences.| | | [](http://links.johnkasich.com/s/c/FoEo9hlan47iBQiOUPaxA-0iEUfscD3E7RsppbIIqK1vhQoQ6wXskuBDpoin0rmcCinLhsnjtlnz_agl1FcPFDg2cY2FEY-10XaFJFTOrScdpWvFoCR7BbmWtBCfApz95CY0aDSqv-dnzWmWQCkOyrDlTlXcMwBY0mFgU4Kzhg18BaaGyaW_mjmawvDyPOvNlkxhqmJET6v5UBiGHCZ79t8YAE3_WW018X8hnewbEDFhqpnvM2QcjrI4K6Zq8grnxUcysbkRwxDYOljU_mIbi007W8Ex11Rt9KFCh1Fqzshe6FAp1A4rFgGmTh2T4V9ixF3jNvVzpo2ws3BZtx-w-PYq3F1wsJ8V3LfEiHsCagWJQWvaOYY_yXiGdidz/_lOtSYrtWdkoTULzPE6ccDUslodphorf/16)
---
Peter, I spent 18 years in Congress, and every one of those years I served on the U.S. House Armed Services Committee. Over that time, I learned something fundamental about the use of American military power. When the United States takes military action, it must be in the direct interest of the United States. That standard matters not just for the moment, but for the long-term order of the world.

That is why I have been troubled by recent events in Venezuela.

Let me be clear. Nicolás Maduro is a very bad guy. He ignored an election that would have removed him from power and ruled as a brutal dictator. Reasonable people can agree on that. But agreeing that someone is terrible does not automatically justify direct U.S. military intervention. There are a lot of very bad actors in this world who do a lot of bad things. The hard question is deciding where and when American force is necessary to protect our national security.

I do not believe that case has been clearly made here.
---
[](http://links.johnkasich.com/s/c/9DIreYPFsk8gTvwBBDgYkNeXIYqpKh6XTMAd60GysVjdzXdgC0vk8CAJXusww-pPsSfVNzQaocai5wVnIETpW4CaCLrbrmWXPmANpNzGtwT1kwvOY4BIIZPcDkYcqmx2Z_SVgotGDbimDdSQp0EMQXNRozQmUdC_4uF9bSuWMMSvqP8yq2MfZgNhZ5O-ZkevYmb9pZ0wHCLkqto013lEMr8tsqpPKsAlNFVAJHRQ9KfRPtfYlXJimj_LvsaLVPISlpAg7Cn5zkBn3DNxFfP2mZrF3g38_SMGNjua1YcWjFxhMbb2cXub_kyNKha9aqjivmaTLAyFVYBG3Aa_ohiIqXFtw7vCKzybBXD1WRBPZNgyits6OtJrOtezFpBUczvIYIdUq1cBtHScjhiuGj1oDStQp9Rm/8TokcPkme5fG4UPXMOwPx_mAWq8cJkCJ/16)
---
Some will inevitably compare this to the U.S. intervention in Panama against Manuel Noriega, and while there are similarities, that episode itself sparked serious debate about precedent, proportionality, and long-term consequences.

When you use the U.S. military to intervene in another country, it is a very serious matter. It requires clear objectives, congressional engagement, and a sober assessment of consequences. At a minimum, senior leaders in Congress, the people who lead the armed services and defense appropriations committees, should have been fully informed. The steady erosion of Congress’s role in decisions of war and peace should concern all of us.

But my deeper concern goes beyond process. It goes to precedent.

We have heard the argument that Venezuela falls within our sphere of influence. That is a dangerous way to think. Once we claim that powerful countries can act militarily simply because another nation lies in their neighborhood, we invite others to do the same.

Does China then say that Taiwan is within its sphere of influence? Does Russia argue that this logic justifies its invasion of Ukraine, and perhaps other countries as well? In fact, that is exactly the argument Vladimir Putin has already made.

Even when an action appears successful in the short term, we have to ask what it means for the long term. Does it embolden other powerful nations to take matters into their own hands. Does it weaken the international rules that govern the global order and help preserve peace.

Those rules exist for a reason. They are meant to restrain the strong, protect the vulnerable, and prevent a world where might makes right. Undermining them, even when intentions seem good, carries real risks.

Some argue that issues like drug trafficking justify military action. Drugs flowing into the United States are a serious problem, no question. But we can point to many countries where drugs originate or move through, including Mexico and Colombia. The core question remains whether this rises to a direct and immediate threat to our national security that requires military force. I do not believe that threshold has been met.

There are other tools available. Economic pressure. Diplomatic isolation. Coordinated international action. These approaches can be effective without crossing the line into direct military intervention. These are complicated matters, and there are rarely simple answers. But complexity is not an excuse for abandoning restraint.

I have seen the costs of intervention firsthand. I remember U.S. troops in Lebanon, where we lost Americans when the Marine barracks were bombed, a mission I never supported. I have questioned whether large scale deployments of boots on the ground, including aspects of Afghanistan, were the right approach, or whether more limited and targeted actions would have better served our goals.

So yes, I hope any intervention produces good outcomes for the United States and for the world. I truly do. But hope is not a strategy.

What troubles me most is the precedent we set and the signal we send. When America acts, others are watching and learning. If we loosen the rules for ourselves, we should not be surprised when others follow suit.

The use of American military power must always be guided by clear national interest, respect for international order, and a deep awareness of long-term consequences. Anything less risks undermining the very stability we seek to protect.

clean_body: When you use the U.S. military to intervene in another country, it is a very serious matter. It requires clear objectives, congressional engagement, and a sober assessment of consequences.| | | Peter, I spent 18 years in Congress, and every one of those years I served on the U.S. House Armed Services Committee. Over that time, I learned something fundamental about the use of American military power. When the United States takes military action, it must be in the direct interest of the United States. That standard matters not just for the moment, but for the long-term order of the world. That is why I have been troubled by recent events in Venezuela. Let me be clear. Nicolás Maduro is a very bad guy. He ignored an election that would have removed him from power and ruled as a brutal dictator. Reasonable people can agree on that. But agreeing that someone is terrible does not automatically justify direct U.S. military intervention. There are a lot of very bad actors in this world who do a lot of bad things. The hard question is deciding where and when American force is necessary to protect our national security. I do not believe that case has been clearly made here. Some will inevitably compare this to the U.S. intervention in Panama against Manuel Noriega, and while there are similarities, that episode itself sparked serious debate about precedent, proportionality, and long-term consequences. When you use the U.S. military to intervene in another country, it is a very serious matter. It requires clear objectives, congressional engagement, and a sober assessment of consequences. At a minimum, senior leaders in Congress, the people who lead the armed services and defense appropriations committees, should have been fully informed. The steady erosion of Congress’s role in decisions of war and peace should concern all of us. But my deeper concern goes beyond process. It goes to precedent. We have heard the argument that Venezuela falls within our sphere of influence. That is a dangerous way to think. Once we claim that powerful countries can act militarily simply because another nation lies in their neighborhood, we invite others to do the same. Does China then say that Taiwan is within its sphere of influence? Does Russia argue that this logic justifies its invasion of Ukraine, and perhaps other countries as well? In fact, that is exactly the argument Vladimir Putin has already made. Even when an action appears successful in the short term, we have to ask what it means for the long term. Does it embolden other powerful nations to take matters into their own hands. Does it weaken the international rules that govern the global order and help preserve peace. Those rules exist for a reason. They are meant to restrain the strong, protect the vulnerable, and prevent a world where might makes right. Undermining them, even when intentions seem good, carries real risks. Some argue that issues like drug trafficking justify military action. Drugs flowing into the United States are a serious problem, no question. But we can point to many countries where drugs originate or move through, including Mexico and Colombia. The core question remains whether this rises to a direct and immediate threat to our national security that requires military force. I do not believe that threshold has been met. There are other tools available. Economic pressure. Diplomatic isolation. Coordinated international action. These approaches can be effective without crossing the line into direct military intervention. These are complicated matters, and there are rarely simple answers. But complexity is not an excuse for abandoning restraint. I have seen the costs of intervention firsthand. I remember U.S. troops in Lebanon, where we lost Americans when the Marine barracks were bombed, a mission I never supported. I have questioned whether large scale deployments of boots on the ground, including aspects of Afghanistan, were the right approach, or whether more limited and targeted actions would have better served our goals. So yes, I hope any intervention produces good outcomes for the United States and for the world. I truly do. But hope is not a strategy. What troubles me most is the precedent we set and the signal we send. When America acts, others are watching and learning. If we loosen the rules for ourselves, we should not be surprised when others follow suit. The use of American military power must always be guided by clear national interest, respect for international order, and a deep awareness of long-term consequences. Anything less risks undermining the very stability we seek to protect. Peter, I plan to remain engaged on this issue because these questions matter for our country’s future. Your support helps make it possible to continue this work in a serious and sustained way. Stay tuned for more updates! I'm so appreciative to have you on the team. Friend,

World War II was over. And while it seemed like good had triumphed over evil, a new specter had darkened the horizon.

As a Royal Air Force pilot who served in the Battle of Britain, Atlas Network's founder, Antony Fisher, had fought against totalitarian collectivism.

But as he settled into a busy life running a farming business, he watched in horror as more countries, including his own in Britain, imposed socialist economic policies.

After reading F. A. Hayek's _The Road to Serfdom_ , he saw the signs of his country being led down the road to serfdom. The book also showed Fisher that he was not alone, which led him to establish a free-market think tank in London a decade later.

It took time, but the Institute for Economic Affairs (IEA) was hugely successful. However, he knew the battle for freedom couldn't be won from a single place.

**In 1981, Anthony Fisher founded Atlas Network, not as another think tank, but as _a force multiplier for freedom_.**

But even as Atlas Network strengthens the worldwide freedom movement, the forces of totalitarian collectivism persist. From creeping authoritarianism to rising state control over markets and speech, the threats to freedom are real and growing.

Today, that single idea has blossomed into a worldwide movement.

Atlas Network empowers 494 pro-freedom partner organizations across 103 countries -- each one working to advance free enterprise, individual freedom, and the rule of law in their own communities and countries.

We train local leaders, connect them with the larger worldwide freedom movement, and support reforms through our trademark _**Coach, Compete, Celebrate**_ strategic model.

**We coach them to become better change agents; we provide investments in their projects on a competitive basis; and we celebrate each achievement.**

That model inspires our partners to improve their performance and to achieve victories for freedom and extraordinary outcomes for their communities.

Every win for freedom is a step toward achieving a more peaceful and prosperous world.

And yet the fight is far from over.
